Title: Japan releases tips on bear spray use amid concern over attacks
Article:
TOKYO: The Japanese government recently released guidelines on how to check the specifications of bear repellent sprays and properly choose and use them amid a proliferation of ineffective products on the market, Kyodo News reported.
With public interest in bear sprays growing as the country faces an increase in bear sightings and attacks, the Environment Ministry and the Consumer Affairs Agency have urged manufacturers and distributors to provide information on the efficacy of their products.
Unlike the United States, Japan has no uniform standards for such sprays.
According to the ministry and other sources, the main component in a repellent is capsaicin, the active chemical compound in chilli peppers.
The concentration of the ingredient in the product should be around 1 to 2 per cent, while the spray should have a range of at least 7.5 metres and a continuous spray duration of at least six seconds, according to the ministry's guidance.
"Some products rebranded for bears were actually made for use against people," said Shinjiro Sasaki, a ministry official who also recommended that people practice using the repellents.
The recently released warnings also urged people not to carry bear sprays unless necessary, to purchase products with a safety latch and to store them out of reach of children.
There were more than 50,000 bear encounters in the year ended March, a record high and double the year-earlier level, according to government data.
"Using the repellent sprays should be a last resort," Environment Minister Hirotaka Ishihara said at a press conference.
"We ask people to also take other countermeasures such as moving in large groups."

Title: At flood-destroyed China-Nepal border, no sign of a once-busy port
Article:
ABOUT 20 Chinese rescue workers in bright orange operated excavators, shovels and ground-penetrating radar detectors on Sunday in an effort to find hundreds of people missing since a tsunami-like mudslide destroyed China's main border crossing with Nepal.
The Gyirong border crossing separating China's Tibet and Nepal became a grisly emblem of the devastation that followed the collapse of a glacier on the Nepal side of the border on Aug 26.
Reuters and other news agencies visited the land port, which sits in a narrow river gorge, in the first trip organised for foreign media by China's foreign ministry.
There was no trace of the five-storey Chinese customs building that had stood at the border before the disaster, video and pictures from the scene showed.
The only structure still visible from before the mudslide was a portion of a nearby water tower installation.
Workers had placed a Chinese flag at the spot where the border gate, at nearly 20-meters-tall, once stood.
Behind hazard signs that read "Danger Area Pass Quickly", three groups of about 20 rescue and recovery workers dug the earth using shovels while several red excavators stood by on Sunday afternoon.
Rescue workers have divided the search area into seven zones, officials told Reuters. They have completed searches in four of them, with three remaining.
[[nid:1526942]]
The mudslide has killed more than 1,300 people on both sides of the border, with more than 5,000 missing.
On Saturday, emergency crews in Nepal rescued a Chinese worker who had been in a tunnel linked to a hydropower station.
On China's side of the border, 31 people had been confirmed dead while 531 others were still classified as missing as of Friday.
Among those still unaccounted for are 261 foreigners from 23 countries, Chinese officials have said.
Gyirong County sits at an average altitude of more than 4,000 meters, though the port itself lies lower, at around 1,800 meters.
The risk of landslides, poor weather and deep mud has further complicated rescue and recovery efforts.
The only land route into Gyirong was restored by Wednesday morning, allowing China to bring in heavy equipment to aid recovery and eventual rebuilding.
State media has shown workers restoring power to the area by sinking temporary electric poles to reconnect it to the grid.
[[nid:1526941]]
Gyirong has emerged as the main border crossing for travelers and trade between Nepal and Tibet over the past decade, after a 2015 earthquake in Nepal badly damaged an alternative crossing farther east.
The port was shut down between July last year and January because of an earlier glacial flood.
In addition to a shipment point to Nepal for Chinese goods, including electric cars, it had also become a crossing point for thousands of Hindu pilgrims in recent years.
Many Hindus travel through Nepal to Mount Kailash, a high-altitude site in Tibet revered by Hindus and Buddhists. Hindus believe it to be the eternal home of Lord Shiva and his wife Parvati.
Many of the foreign nationals still missing in Tibet were pilgrims with extended families in India, diplomats in Beijing have said.
There are 49 Indian citizens among the missing.
* The writers are from Reuters

Title: Police step up highway monitoring as motorists return home after school holidays
Article:
SLUG: POLHI
Police step up highway monitoring as motorists return home after school holidays
Austin Camoens
austin@nst.com.my
KUALA LUMPUR: Police are closely monitoring major highways nationwide as motorists begin making their way home following the school holidays.
Bukit Aman Traffic Enforcement and Investigation Department (TEID) director Datuk Seri Mohammed Hasbullah Ali said highway patrol units were on the ground monitoring traffic conditions and ensuring the safety of road users.
He said police expected an increase in the number of vehicles on major highways as families returned home ahead of the resumption of school and work.
"Our highway patrol units are on the ground and we are monitoring the situation, particularly along the major highways.
"We urge motorists to plan their journeys properly, remain patient and, most importantly, obey traffic regulations throughout their journey," he told the New Straits Times today.
Hasbullah reminded motorists not to rush despite potentially heavier traffic and longer travelling times.
He said drivers should ensure they were sufficiently rested before embarking on long-distance journeys and stop at a safe location to rest if they began feeling tired or sleepy.
"Do not force yourself to continue driving when you are tired. Fatigue can affect your concentration and reaction time.
"Motorists should also avoid speeding, tailgating or making dangerous lane changes simply to save a few minutes on their journey," he said.
Hasbullah also reminded motorists not to use mobile phones while driving, stressing that their attention should remain on the road at all times.
He advised motorists to check their vehicles before travelling, particularly the tyres, brakes, lights and other essential components, to reduce the risk of breakdowns or accidents.
Motorists, he added, should wear their seat belts, while motorcyclists and pillion riders must use properly fastened helmets.
He also urged road users to exercise patience in congested areas and refrain from misusing the emergency lane.
"Give way to ambulances, police, fire and rescue vehicles and other emergency vehicles when necessary," he said.
Hasbullah said motorists should also maintain a safe following distance, use their indicators before changing lanes and observe speed limits.
He urged road users to take extra precautions during bad weather, including reducing their speed and increasing the distance between their vehicles and the one ahead.
"Everyone wants to reach home safely. There is no need to rush or take unnecessary risks.
"Be courteous to other road users, follow the rules and make safety your priority throughout the journey," he said.

Title: Komuniti Madani must be stronger bridge between government and people, says Wan Azizah
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Komuniti Madani initiative should play a greater role as a bridge between the government and the people, Bandar Tun Razak member of Parliament Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail said.
She said this role was crucial to ensure that every government policy and initiative reached its intended targets, while also effectively channelling public feedback to the relevant agencies for further action.
"Do not merely be information transmitters; be attentive listeners to the issues affecting the elderly, families in distress and the needs of the youth," she said at the Komuniti Madani appointment certificate ceremony for the Bandar Tun Razak parliamentary constituency here today.
Also present were the Prime Minister's political secretary Datuk Azman Abidin, Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya Federal Territories Information Department director Normaizatulakmal Tujad, and Bandar Tun Razak Komuniti Madani chairman Jonathan Vela.
The Prime Minister's wife said that as the government's eyes and ears, community members must be proactive in following up on issues faced by the public.
She said while Komuniti Madani might not be able to resolve every issue raised, the network must ensure that each concern reached those with the authority and responsibility to act.
Meanwhile, she said the initiative must also serve as a frontline defence against the spread of false information, particularly in the age of social media.
"Misinformation spreads rapidly and can disrupt harmony. Komuniti Madani must be the first line of defence against falsehoods, adhering to the principle: 'Check before sharing'.
"We may have differing views, but we must always maintain mutual respect," she said.
Dr Wan Azizah said the true strength of any community lay in the relationships between neighbours and the willingness of people of diverse races and backgrounds to help and support one another.
In this regard, Dr Wan Azizah said the appointees must uphold trust and integrity, proactively engage with the community and listen closely to the people's concerns.
At the ceremony, Dr Wan Azizah also presented the Komuniti Madani Ambassador Award to Azizi Anas and S. Yugan, as well as appointment certificates to representatives from six sub-zones within Bandar Tun Razak.
Komuniti Madani is a rebranding of the 1,878 Komuniti Keluarga Malaysia groups following the launch of the Malaysia Madani framework on Jan 19, 2023.
In the Federal Territories of Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya, 72 Komuniti Madani groups have been established, with the network's strength depending on volunteers who dedicate their time and energy to serving the community.

Title: PPP open to BN-Pas cooperation, but wants to weigh pros and cons
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The People's Progressive Party (PPP) is open to the idea of cooperation between Barisan Nasional (BN) and Pas, but wants to assess its pros and cons before taking a position.
Its president, Datuk Dr Loga Bala Mohan, said the party also needed to determine how such cooperation could benefit BN.
"When you talk about cooperation or understanding, they are 2 different things. So, Umno-Pas cooperation is something to do with race and religion. So, we cannot interfere in race and religion issues.
"However, in terms of having BN, it is a different story. We have to see the pros and cons. So, our stand will be that we are open to the idea to listen and see how it can benefit," he told reporters after chairing the party's Supreme Council meeting at its headquarters today.
Loga Bala was responding to a question on PPP's stand following remarks by former Elected Representatives Council (Mubarak) president Datuk Mohd Rozali Isohak that growing cooperation between Pas and Umno should be sustained at least until the 16th General Election (GE16).
He said any such cooperation would also have to take into account concerns among non-Malays and non-Muslims over Pas' presence.
"Generally, there is a fear. There is nothing else but fear among non-Malays and non-Muslims, who think that Pas' existence will cause a big dent in their lifestyle.
"So, the onus will fall on Pas on how to eradicate that fear and encourage them to come and join the rest of Malaysians.
"I don't think there is an issue with the Malay-Muslim community, but the non-Muslim community in Malaysia will have this problem."
On Sept 5, Rozali, a former Kelantan deputy Menteri Besar, said such cooperation
should have taken place long ago
.
Rozali said the cooperation could strengthen Malay and Muslim unity after years of waiting for the 2 major Malay-based parties to work together.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Firemen put out Klang bush fire amid open-burning surge
Article:
KLANG: Firemen extinguished a bush fire at Taman Eng Ann here this morning.
Selangor Fire and Rescue Department assistant director of operations Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the department received an emergency call at 11.05am about the fire in Jalan Murai.
"A team of seven firemen from the Klang Utara Fire and Rescue station was dispatched to the scene and arrived at 11.11am.
"The fire involved a 50ft by 30ft area of bushes.
"Firemen managed to extinguish the blaze and the operation ended at 11.36am," he said in a statement today.
No casualties were reported.
https://www.nst.com.my/news/nation/2026/09/1526537/negligence-all-it-takes-spark-huge-fire-warns-fire-dept
The New Straits Times reported that a carelessly discarded cigarette butt, an unattended pile of burning rubbish or a small fire used to clear land could ignite a major bush or peat fire during this current hot and dry spell.
Fire and Rescue Department director-general Datuk Seri Nor Hisham Mohamad said prolonged dry weather had stripped moisture from grass, bushes and other vegetation, providing ready fuel for fires.
He said hot weather was not necessarily the cause of major fires but could turn even a minor ignition source into a major blaze.
Nor Hisham said strong winds could spread flames through dry vegetation, widening the area firefighters must contain.
The warning comes following a sharp rise in open-burning incidents nationwide during the recent hot and dry spell.
Cases climbed from 53 on Aug 20 to 70 the following day before jumping to 180 on Aug 22 and peaking at 231 on Aug 23. Another 190 incidents were recorded on Aug 24.

Title: 600 Orang Asli youths pursue higher education, triple target set four years ago
Article:
ISKANDAR PUTERI: More than 600 Orang Asli youths are currently pursuing their studies at universities and colleges nationwide, reflecting the government's concern over education issues affecting the community.
Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the figure had exceeded the initial target of 200 when the Department of Orang Asli Development (Jakoa) was placed under the Rural and Regional Development Ministry, which he heads, four years ago.
"In the first year, the challenge was accepted. It was not just 200 entering universities, but more than 300 Orang Asli youths enrolled in universities that year.
"In the second year, I raised the target to 300.
"Clearly, the achievement of Orang Asli youths entering universities increased to 400 in the second year," he said when officiating the closing ceremony of the 2026 National Orang Asli Sports Carnival at the EduCity Sports Complex here today.
Also present was Johor Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi.
Zahid said the achievement of more than 600 students this year proved that the Orang Asli community had the ability to progress further if given the opportunity and appropriate educational support.
"This is good social mobility because education is an element that can improve the social status of any community in the world," he said.
He said efforts to empower education among the Orang Asli community had also been expanded to Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET), including through the provision of specialised institutions for the community.
Zahid said one such institution was the Paya Bungor Training Centre in Maran, Pahang, which currently has 135 Orang Asli youths enrolled in TVET programmes offering both short and long-term courses.
He also commended the Johor government's commitment to allocating RM600,000 to 60 Orang Asli villages in the state, equivalent to RM10,000 for each village.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: OPEC+ set to keep oil output policy unchanged, sources say
Article:
BENGALURU: OPEC+ is set to keep its oil output policy unchanged for October at a meeting on Sunday, two people familiar with the discussions told Reuters, as the producer group needs to agree on new quotas before deciding its next output steps.
The meeting comes as the Iran war continues to disrupt oil exports through the Strait of Hormuz, limiting OPEC+'s influence over prices and market share. Unlike in the past, the group's supply decisions have had a limited impact on the market.
In August, OPEC+ agreed to increase production in September, completing a phased rollback of a 1.65 million-barrel-per-day supply cut first agreed in 2023.
Despite the agreed production increases, the group, made up of the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries and its allies, including Russia, still produces far below its targets because of the war.
OPEC+ still has another layer of production cuts in place, covering most members of the 21-country group until the end of 2026.
Before the group decides how to unwind the cuts and return production to the market, it needs to review members' oil production capacity to set 2027 output baselines, which form the basis for quotas.
This debate will likely happen later in 2026, and hence OPEC+ is likely to pause its output increases for the fourth quarter, sources earlier told Reuters.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar, Al Gore discuss climate crisis, Malaysia's energy transition
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim contacted former United States vice-president Al Gore to discuss the global climate crisis and Malaysia's efforts to mitigate its environmental impact.
Anwar said they also discussed the haze affecting Malaysia following forest fires in Indonesia.
"The discussion also covered Malaysia's commitment and ongoing measures to accelerate the country's energy transition from fossil fuels to cleaner, more sustainable energy sources.
"These efforts are in line with the government's commitment to building a country that is progressive and economically resilient, while preserving environmental sustainability for the well-being of future generations," he said in a Facebook post.
Anwar added that he had invited Gore to visit Malaysia soon to continue discussions and explore avenues for closer cooperation on tackling climate change and advancing the country's energy transition agenda.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: PPP urges BN to push for early GE16
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Barisan Nasional (BN) should push for the 16th general election (GE16) to be held as soon as possible to restore political stability, said the People's Progressive Party (PPP).
Its president, Datuk Dr Loga Bala Mohan, said the country was already experiencing "election fever" following the recent elections in Johor and Negeri Sembilan, with the Melaka election expected to be next.
"We are seeing a lot of instability, and this needs to be addressed before things get out of hand. We urge BN to seek to have the general election held as soon as possible," he told reporters after chairing the party's Supreme Council meeting at its headquarters today.
Recently, Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi voiced support for
an earlier GE16
, saying it would allow the government to seek a fresh mandate.
Zahid, who is also BN chairman, said the coalition was nevertheless prepared to face the polls if Parliament served its full term.
The 15th Parliament is due to complete its full term on Dec 18 next year.
Meanwhile, Loga Bala said he hoped the government would consider the higher costs involved in holding state elections separately from the general election.
"This involves taxpayers' money. If the elections are held simultaneously, the cost can be reduced," he said.
He said holding the elections simultaneously would also be in line with the Madani government's previous pledge to reduce wastage in the use of public funds.
"Reducing the cost of elections is one way this can be achieved," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: M40 group among focus of Budget 2027 initiatives – Finance Minister's aide
Article:
LUMUT: Budget 2027 is expected to place particular emphasis on efforts to address socioeconomic issues, including the welfare of the middle-income (M40) and lower-income groups, according to an aide of the Finance Minister.
Muhammad Kamil Abdul Munim, who is political secretary to Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, said the focus on both groups was necessary as they are among those most affected by economic pressures and current cost-of-living challenges.
"The Budget to be announced by the Prime Minister will be another more inclusive Budget, one that is closer to the people and can, to some extent, resolve several problems and issues that have arisen.
"For now, the parties involved are still conducting direct engagement sessions with all stakeholders to finalise the Budget," he said.
He said this when met after officiating the National Khatam Keris Traditional Ceremony organised by the Perak branch of the Persatuan Silat Seni Gayong Malaysia and the Silat Anak-Anak Gayong Perak Gathering at Teluk Batik Campsite here today.
Anwar, who is Prime Minister and Finance Minister, is scheduled to table Budget 2027 in the Dewan Rakyat on Oct 9.
Muhammad Kamil said existing initiatives such as the Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA) would continue to be strengthened to ease the financial burden on households.
"Assistance programmes such as STR and SARA will continue, and we await further announcements by the Finance Minister," he said.
Muhammad Kamil said consideration was also being given to proposals to improve existing initiatives and introduce other forms of financial support to ease the burden on middle-income households.
"The government's priorities also remain focused on ensuring that political and economic stability remains strong to guarantee the smooth implementation of national policies," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Zahid: Cloud seeding extended to improve deteriorating air quality in Sarawak
Article:
ISKANDAR PUTERI: The cloud seeding operation was extended across Sarawak to help improve air quality following the haze enveloping several parts of the state.
Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said two divisions, Kuching and Sri Aman, recorded very unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of this morning.
He, who is also National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma) chairman, said the situation in Serian, which was declared a state of emergency yesterday, had begun to show positive developments, with API readings continuing to decline.
"We hope that in conjunction with the Malaysia Day celebrations in Kuching, the cloud seeding operations will help lower the air pollution index, particularly in Sarawak."
Zahid, who is also rural and regional development minister, said this after attending the closing ceremony of the 2026 National Orang Asli Sports Carnival at the Educity Sports Complex here today.
Earlier, Nadma director-general Datuk Meor Ismail Meor Akim had said that cloud seeding operations were being carried out across Sarawak until tomorrow to mitigate the haze affecting the state.
His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, the King of Malaysia, on Friday consented to declaring
a state of emergency
throughout the Serian division after the area recorded hazardous API readings of more than 500 at the time.
However, checks showed that Serian recorded an unhealthy API reading of 183 as of 3.15pm today.
According to the Environment Department's Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), 35 other air quality monitoring stations, including 10 in Sarawak, also recorded API readings in the same category.
Only Kuching recorded a very unhealthy API reading, at 218.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Women passengers should have option to choose female e-hailing drivers — Loke
Article:
Women passengers should have option to choose female e-hailing drivers — Loke
PUTRAJAYA: E-hailing companies are encouraged to offer female driver options for women passengers to improve their safety and comfort, says Transport Minister Anthony Loke.
He said the option would give women passengers an alternative that prioritised their well-being when using e-hailing services.
"This is a feature that I hope our women leaders can promote. When using e-hailing services, one of the available options should be the ability to choose a female driver," he said in his speech at the Wanita DAP National Congress 2026 here today, in his capacity as the party's secretary-general.
Loke said he had also urged e-hailing companies to introduce women-only carpooling options.
"I suggested that carpooling should include a women-only option, allowing female passengers to share rides only with other women," he said.
On rail services, Loke said safety measures continued to be strengthened through women-only coaches following frequent complaints to the ministry about sexual harassment, particularly during peak hours.
He said women accounted for nearly two-thirds of rail passengers, making their safety a priority.
Meanwhile, Loke said efforts to empower women in the transport sector included creating more opportunities in traditionally male-dominated fields such as aviation and maritime.
He said gender stereotypes in these sectors must be challenged to ensure women were given opportunities based on their abilities.
"We believe that if men can fly aircraft, women can do the same. If women can drive, why can't they fly aircraft? These stereotypes must be changed," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Cloud seeding extended as Sarawak battles haze
Article:
KUCHING: Cloud seeding operations across Sarawak have been extended until tomorrow as efforts continue to mitigate transboundary haze affecting the state.
Sarawak Disaster Management Committee (SDMC) chairman Datuk Amar Douglas Uggah Embas said the extension followed a successful operation yesterday, which brought rainfall to the targeted areas around Bakun and Murum dams.
"Today's operation will continue as planned and will be carried out where suitable cloud and weather conditions permit," he said in a statement today.
Sarawak has been conducting cloud seeding operations targeting key dams and water catchment areas in the state since Thursday.
Meanwhile, Uggah said air quality in Serian had shown an improving trend, with the air pollutant index (API) reading at 185 as at noon today, placing it in the unhealthy category.
"There is a downward trend for the API level in Serian as we enter the second of three days of monitoring. The API is primarily affected by wind direction and the source of hotspots," he said.
He said continued monitoring was necessary before any formal recommendation on Serian's emergency status could be submitted to Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg and Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
Uggah said data from the Asean Specialised Meteorological Centre (ASMC) showed there were no hotspots in Sarawak, while 184 were detected in neighbouring Kalimantan, Indonesia.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Toddler placed in induced coma after stray dog attack
Article:
BATU PAHAT: A 2-year-old girl was critically injured after being attacked by a pack of stray dogs in front of her grandmother's house at Kampung Tambak, Sungai Kelambu, Peserai, here yesterday.
In the 7am incident, Nur Haira Watikah Mohammad Hamizi suffered severe head and facial injuries after being set upon by five dogs.
Her grandmother, Darlinda Darlis, 56, said the toddler was left in her care after her parents left for Johor Baru for work.
"Nur Haira was lying beside her older brother and sister, drinking milk while I was getting ready to take a bath.
"After my bath, I looked for Nur Haira and saw the front door open. I went outside and was shocked to see five dogs biting her," she said when met today.
Darlinda said her cries alerted her son, who rushed out to rescue the child, who was covered in blood.
Darlinda said she and her son immediately took Nur Haira to Sultanah Nora Ismail Hospital (HSNI), where she was treated in the red zone and placed in an induced coma.
"I cannot describe how she looked at the time. Her eyes were open, but she could not speak. I cried throughout the journey because I could not bear seeing her in that condition.
"Soon after, she was transferred to Sultanah Aminah Hospital (HSA) in Johor Baru due to the severity of her injuries," she said.
Darlinda also claimed the stray dogs were abandoned by hunters who used them to hunt wild boar in a nearby oil palm plantation.
"They use these dogs for hunting and leave them here after they are done. We have been worried about the stray dogs for a long time because their numbers keep increasing," she said.
Meanwhile, Batu Pahat district police chief Assistant Commissioner Shahrulanuar Mushaddat Abdullah Sani confirmed that police had received a report on the incident.
He said the case was being investigated under the Child Act 2001.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: KLIA sets up rest areas for passengers affected by Jakarta airport closure
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) has urged passengers travelling to Jakarta on affected flights to contact their airlines for the latest schedule updates after volcanic ash from Anak Krakatau forced the temporary closure of Soekarno-Hatta International Airport.
In a travel advisory, KLIA confirmed the ash-related closure and said via social media that resting areas had been set up for affected passengers awaiting further updates.
"At Terminal 1, designated resting areas are at Anjung Tinjau, Level 5 of the Main Terminal Building; the CRS Area, Level 3 of the Main Terminal Building; and Gate C36, Mezzanine Level of the Satellite Building.
"At Terminal 2, the resting area is at Level 3A (Mezzanine Floor), Departure Hall," it said.
Anak Krakatau, located in the Sunda Strait between Java and Sumatra, continued erupting on Saturday, with authorities reporting lava-fountaining activity and booming and rumbling sounds heard from an observation post.
The eruption began at 11.07pm local time on Friday and continued during observations from midnight to 6am on Saturday.
Indonesia's Centre for Volcanology and Geological Hazard Mitigation said the volcano remained at Level III, or Siaga (Alert), with a three-kilometre exclusion zone around its active crater.
Authorities said the volcano's regrown edifice was relatively small and was not considered capable of collapsing on a scale that could trigger a tsunami.S

Title: No SJKT will be closed, assures Fadhlina
Article:
NIBONG TEBAL: No national-type Tamil school (SJKT) will be closed down, with all such schools continuing to receive support for development, maintenance and programmes to strengthen teachers and students.
Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said the assurance was necessary to address persistent misperceptions within the community that certain SJKTs would be shut down.
"I stand by this assurance because there are still those in our community who believe these schools will be closed.
"As the Madani government, we give our assurance that no SJKT will be closed. In fact, we will focus on all schools for development, maintenance, and programs to strengthen teachers and students," she said.
She was speaking at the presentation of the Letter of Acceptance and groundbreaking ceremony for the SJKT Sungai Bakap construction project here today.
Fadhlina said the new RM12.6 million school building is vital for the local community and the education of children in the area.
The project will be implemented by Yayasan Didik Negara (YDN) over 56 weeks, with monitoring by the Penang State Education Department.
"This school is designed to meet children's needs comprehensively and will serve an important educational purpose, not only at the local level but also for the nation," she said, while thanking parents, teachers, and community leaders for their support.
Penang Special Committee on Tamil Schools chairman Datuk Seri S. Sundarajoo said the project had faced delays and was halted for over seven years due to land matters, contractor issues, and court cases, all of which have now been resolved.
He said the new building is urgently needed as the current school building, which houses more than 100 pupils, is dilapidated.
"Development is targeted for completion within 56 weeks. Foundation work, which is among the most time-consuming components, is underway, and the next stage will involve the main structure," said Sundarajoo, who is also the state Housing and Environment Committee chairman.
He added that the state government aims to construct three SJKT buildings this year. SJKT Sungai Bakap is the second, while construction on the third, SJKT Juru, is expected to begin before the end of the year.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: CJ heads list of 128 Terengganu honours recipients
Article:
KUALA TERENGGANU: Chief Justice Tun Wan Ahmad Farid Wan Salleh topped the list of 128 recipients of Terengganu state honours and medals in conjunction with the 64th birthday celebration of Sultan Terengganu Sultan Mizan Zainal Abidin.
The Regent of Terengganu, Tengku Muhammad Ismail Sultan Mizan Zainal Abidin, officiated the investiture ceremony at the Balairong Seri of Istana Syarqiyyah here.
Also present were his siblings, Tengku Seri Setia Mahkota Raja Tengku Datuk Seri Muhammad Muaz, Tengku Puteri Utama Raja Tengku Nadhirah Zahrah and Tengku Puteri Daulath Raja Tengku Fatimatuz Zahra', as well as Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar and state government leaders.
Wan Ahmad Farid was conferred the Darjah Kebesaran Seri Setia Sultan Mizan Zainal Abidin Terengganu (S.S.M.Z), which carries the title Datuk Seri.
Also receiving the S.S.M.Z were Qatar Ambassador to Malaysia Datuk Seri Salah Mohammed Al-Sorour, Chief of Air Force General Tan Sri Muhamad Norazlan Aris and Terengganu Equestrian Association deputy president Tan Sri Abdullah Taib.
Tengku Muhammad Ismail also conferred the Darjah Kebesaran Datuk Setia Sultan Mizan Zainal Abidin Terengganu (D.S.M.Z), which carries the title Datuk, on Federal Court judge Datuk Che Mohd Ruzima Ghazali and CelcomDigi Bhd board adviser and former chief executive officer Datuk Mohamad Idham Nawawi.
Also receiving the D.S.M.Z were Mirmas Holding Sdn Bhd executive chairman Datuk Awalan Abdul Aziz and Messrs Feroz@Co managing partner Datuk Feroz A S Moidunny.

They included actor Datuk Abdul Manan Embong, better known as Eman Manan, and Terengganu Tourism, Culture, Environment and Climate Change Committee chairman Datuk Razali Idris.
Also receiving the D.P.M.T were Dungun MP Datuk Wan Hassan Mohd Ramli, Universiti Malaysia Terengganu vice-chancellor Professor Datuk Dr Mohd Zamri Ibrahim and Terengganu police chief Datuk Mohd Khairi Khairudin.
Tengku Muhammad Ismail also conferred the Darjah Kebesaran Setia Sultan Mizan Zainal Abidin Terengganu (S.M.Z) on 17 recipients, including Terengganu Information, Dakwah and Syariah Empowerment Committee chairman Muhammad Khalil Abdul Hadi.

Title: UN must transform into 'UN 2.0' to remain relevant, says Jokowi
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Former Indonesian president Joko Widodo has stressed that the United Nations must reform and redefine its systems, processes and strategies into a new version, "UN 2.0".
He said this was necessary to ensure the global institution remains relevant in addressing increasingly complex challenges facing the world.
He noted that change was crucial as global issues grow more complicated, with interconnected conflicts frequently crossing national borders.
"Today, the challenges we face are increasingly complicated, conflicts are interconnected and their consequences cross borders.
"Therefore, the UN must change and redefine its systems, processes and strategies to build a better world and remain relevant.
"As we need stronger global institutions, more effective global mediation and more robust global diplomacy to maintain peace, we must now move beyond the old version of the UN and build a new version, UN 2.0.
"This is because lasting prosperity can only be achieved when every nation chooses peace over conflict, cooperation over competition, and collaboration over division," he said in his keynote address at the Penang Peace Dialogue 2026 here today.
Touching on global leadership, he cautioned that the rapid advancement of technology, automation and artificial intelligence must be accompanied by wisdom and empathy so as not to divide societies.
"The real question today is no longer about how fast humanity moves, but that we must move forward together, with the courage to adapt, the humility to listen and the commitment to stay connected with our people.
"We also often speak of economic, political and technological power.
"However, true strength lies not only in how much power we hold, but in how deeply we understand one another," he said.
He said genuine leadership in an era of populism requires a balance of competence, integrity, patience, pragmatism, courage and empathy towards society.
Understanding an issue does not begin with official statements or negotiations, but rather with listening, he added.
He held up Southeast Asia as an ideal example where cultural, religious and traditional diversity has been harmonised into a tolerant way of life, serving as a bridge of cross-civilisational cooperation rather than a weakness.
"For centuries, this region has been shaped by the interaction of civilisations, cultures, religions, traditions and ideas.
"Southeast Asia has already become a living example of how diverse civilisations can coexist, learn from one another and grow together," he said.
In this regard, he called on developed nations not to be concerned solely with their own interests, but to shoulder greater responsibility in building global trust, strengthening cooperation, and creating a more peaceful world.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: UPTM students to launch companies before graduation under pilot project
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Universiti Poly-Tech Malaysia (UPTM) students will be guided to set up their own companies before graduating under a pilot project aimed at turning their innovations into viable businesses.
UPTM pro-chancellor Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said the project would be developed with support from Tekun Nasional and Farm Fresh Bhd, which had expressed willingness to help students commercialise their innovations.
He said the initiative was part of UPTM's efforts to increase the proportion of graduates becoming entrepreneurs from seven per cent to at least 40 per cent next year.
"I believe that with the support of the deputy vice-chancellors and the Faculty of Business and Accounting, a special project can be launched.
"Through these innovation projects, we want our undergraduates to register their own companies, initially as e-commerce consultants or firms that can help small and medium enterprises make full use of e-commerce platforms and available innovations," he said.
He was speaking at the First Youth E-Commerce Business Innovation Programme and recognition ceremony for the Malaysia Book of Records title for the "Largest Virtual Participation in an E-Commerce Innovation Platform" here today.
The programme, implemented under the Service Learning Malaysia – University for Society (Sulam) initiative, aims to link academic learning with practical experience in business innovation, digital entrepreneurship and community engagement.
The innovation competition featured three themes — Business, Social and Technology — and received 590 project entries involving 2,232 participants.
The programme also received official recognition from the Malaysia Book of Records under the title "Largest Virtual Participation in an E-Commerce Innovation Platform".
Asyraf said professors had been tasked with monitoring the projects and would have to report on their progress to him within a month of the event.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar: Issues involving Felda subsidiary to be exposed in coming weeks
Article:
SERDANG: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said issues involving a subsidiary of the Federal Land Development Authority (Felda) would be exposed within the next few weeks.
He said the disclosure was aimed at identifying weaknesses within the institution.
"Likewise, in the next few weeks, we will expose the problems involving Felda. Tabung Haji is still under investigation and action.
"Every year, Felda, which is involved in agriculture, plantations and settlers, requires the Finance Ministry to provide RM980 million to service debts arising from its losses.
"Every year, almost RM1 billion in government funds, taxpayers' money, has to be paid. If it is due to a disaster, we understand. But this is due to weak management and the practice of taking the people's rights by those entrusted," he said at the closing of Maha 2026 here today.
Present were Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu and Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari.
Anwar stressed that the situation not only resulted in losses to the government, but also indirectly affected Felda settlers.
"So if RM1 billion does not have to be paid, there is no need for us to make up for it. What do we do? We help the settlers.
"Now, for example, if we want to provide assistance, if we take the option of covering Felda's losses, then Felda pays, not the previous management," he said.
Earlier, Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman did not rule out the possibility that several individuals could be detained in stages starting this week.
This followed allegations of misappropriation, abuse of power and corruption involving a Felda subsidiary.
He said that so far, 12 individuals had been called to assist in investigations into the case.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MPOB charts new course for palm oil industry
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Palm Oil Board (MPOB) is shifting into a more market-driven role, seeking to move beyond research and regulation to actively shape the future of Malaysia's palm oil industry.
This is through greater digitalisation, global engagement and higher-value downstream development.
The transformation is being driven by PALMS 2030, a new framework aimed at strengthening the industry's competitiveness, accelerating technology adoption and expanding Malaysia's strategic presence in key global markets by 2030.
MPOB director-general Datuk Badrul Hisham Mohd said the framework marked a fundamental shift in how the agency operates, with greater emphasis on responding to market needs, leading the industry and translating research capabilities into economic value.
"We can no longer simply respond to issues after they arise. MPOB needs to be closer to the market, act faster and be more willing to drive change," he said at a town hall session with MPOB staff last Friday.
He said PALMS 2030 would be built around five principles -  productivity, automation, low carbon, marketability and sustainability -  and delivered through three core value chains: institutional reform, industry leadership and driving economic growth.
A key priority will be strengthening MPOB's international footprint, including exploring the establishment of regional offices in selected strategic markets to deepen engagement with industry players, research institutions and other international stakeholders.
Badrul said MPOB's research capabilities and technical expertise would also be deployed more strategically to help Malaysia respond to mounting trade challenges.
This includes the European Union Deforestation Regulation as well as anti-dumping and countervailing duties in the United States.
"We want MPOB to be not only a reference centre for palm oil technology, but also the eyes and ears of the industry in strategic global markets," he said.
The transformation will also place greater emphasis on moving Malaysia up the palm oil value chain.
MPOB is strengthening downstream development to reduce reliance on commodity exports and expand higher-value products such as oleochemicals, nutraceuticals and sustainable aviation fuel.
At the smallholder level, MPOB will broaden the role of its Tunas officers through five new functions — technology transfer agents, productivity coaches, innovation leaders, market liaisons and sustainability agents.
Badrul said the expanded role would help smallholders raise productivity, lower production costs, gain better market access and ultimately increase their net income.
The approach will also bring smallholders closer to the wider value chain through Sustainable Palm Oil Growers Cooperatives, while strengthening compliance with Malaysian Sustainable Palm Oil certification.
Under the institutional reform agenda, MPOB aims to digitise at least 90 per cent of its management and administrative processes by 2030, cutting bureaucracy, speeding up services and improving organisational efficiency.
The transformation will be underpinned by a high-performance culture centred on integrity, accountability and zero tolerance for misconduct.
MPOB will also deepen its research and development capabilities by establishing formal collaborations between all its research stations and universities and research institutes locally and internationally.
The partnerships are expected to broaden expertise networks, accelerate knowledge sharing and technology development, and improve the commercialisation of research outcomes.
Beyond the palm oil industry, Badrul said PALMS 2030 was expected to support the creation of high-skilled jobs, attract foreign direct investment, strengthen Malaysia's technological capabilities and contribute to food security.
"When we reform the institution, we can lead the industry. When we lead the industry, we can drive the economy.
"And when the economy is strengthened, the benefits must return to the people and the country," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia Airlines, Batik Air cancel 20 Malaysia-Jakarta flights over volcanic ash
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia Airlines and Batik Air have cancelled a total of 20 flights between Malaysia and Jakarta today after volcanic ash from the ongoing eruption of Mount Anak Krakatau disrupted operations at Jakarta's Soekarno-Hatta International Airport.
In a post on X, Malaysia Airlines said that it had cancelled 12 flights between Kuala Lumpur International Airport and Jakarta.
"Given the evolving situation, Malaysia Airlines is closely monitoring developments.
"Further updates on affected flights will be communicated directly to affected customers," it said.
The national carrier advised passengers to ensure their contact details were updated via "My Booking" on its website to receive updates by email and SMS.
Meanwhile, Batik Air said it had cancelled eight scheduled flights between Malaysia and Jakarta today, with six operating between Kuala Lumpur International Airport and Jakarta and two between Subang and Jakarta.
It said the decision followed close coordination with aviation authorities and airport operators, with passenger and crew safety remaining its priority.
"The presence of volcanic ash in the airspace can reduce visibility, interfere with aircraft navigation systems and potentially compromise engine performance," it said.
Batik Air said it would continue monitoring the situation and provide updates through its official website and social media channels. Affected passengers would also be notified through their registered contact details.
Passengers may request to reschedule their travel to the next available Batik Air flight, subject to availability, or seek a refund.
They are advised to contact Batik Air's Customer Care Centre or their respective booking channels for assistance.
Batik Air, a Malaysian carrier, operates under Indonesia's Lion Air Group.
Earlier today, AirAsia said several flights to and from Jakarta had been
cancelled or rescheduled
due to volcanic ash from Mount Anak Krakatau.
The airline said affected passengers had been notified of their flight status and arrangements made for them to travel on the next available flight.
Anak Krakatau has been erupting since Sept 4, with ash plumes detected at altitudes of up to 50,000 feet in some areas.
The
volcano
lies between Java and Sumatra along the Pacific Ring of Fire, where earthquakes and volcanic eruptions are frequent.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Investigations into corruption not driven by revenge or jealousy, says Anwar
Article:
SERDANG: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has rejected claims that ongoing investigations into corruption, abuse of power and misappropriation are driven by revenge or jealousy.
He said he was not directly involved in investigations conducted by the authorities and that decisions on whether to prosecute any party were under the jurisdiction of the Attorney-General.
Anwar said his role was to ensure the administration of the country operated according to the law, particularly in efforts to curb corruption and abuse of power.
"Some parties claim that this is driven by revenge or jealousy. In reality, I am not the one conducting the investigations. They are carried out by the enforcement agencies.
"The Attorney-General and his team scrutinise every detail of a case before deciding whether to file charges. The judges are the ones who impose sentences.
"My role is simply to ensure that the government operates according to the law and regulations. Misappropriation and corruption must be eradicated, and this is not an ordinary political game," he said.
Anwar said this in his speech at the closing ceremony of the Malaysia Agriculture, Horticulture and Agrotourism Exhibition (Maha) 2026 at the Malaysia Agro Exposition Park Serdang (MAEPS) here today.
He stressed that enforcement action should be based on principles of justice and transparency, regardless of a person's position or rank.
Anwar said the government would continue to uphold the rule of law and ensure that enforcement action was taken based on the merits of each case.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Top US military officials face lie-detectors in leak hunt: Reports
Article:
WASHINGTON: The Pentagon has launched a lie-detector dragnet to comb through high-ranking military officials and identify who leaked information about US munitions stockpiles, according to US press reports.
In July, reports emerged that the United States was rationing munitions – its missile interceptors, in particular – over supply concerns after several months of fighting Iran.
Administration officials vehemently denied those reports, with President Donald Trump saying "we have a lot of ammunition, different types," while acknowledging that "for some of the more sophisticated stuff, we'd certainly like to have more."
Late Friday, The New York Times reported that some 50 members of the military's Joint Staff – the Pentagon's planning and advisory staff – were being required to take polygraph tests as part of an investigation into how classified stockpile information made its way into journalists' hands.
CBS News later also reported the wide-scale use of lie detectors, while adding that the chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, General Dan Caine, had not been tested.
Both outlets cited unnamed officials.
Asked by AFP about the reports, the Pentagon's chief spokesman, Sean Parnell, refused to comment on "internal personnel or investigative matters," but said that it "takes all leaks of classified national security information extremely seriously and investigates accordingly."
"Securing classified information is critical to ensuring the security of the United States and of our troops deployed around the world," Parnell added.
Both the Times and CBS noted the scale of the polygraph testing.
Lie-detection testing is routine during background screenings and security clearance renewals for government staff with access to the most sensitive state secrets.
But the wide-scale deployment of the detectors as part of a leak investigation was rare, if unprecedented, the outlets reported, citing analysts and unnamed officials.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MAFS budget allocation likely to be increased in line with commendable performance – Anwar
Article:
SERDANG: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has hinted that the allocation for the Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security (MAFS) is likely to be increased in Budget 2027, in line with the ministry's commendable performance this year.
He said the commitment was in line with the ministry's role as a key pillar in ensuring the success of programmes to empower the agricultural sector in the country.
"This is because the Madani government is giving special focus to the development of programmes under the ministry, and I think what was urged by Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu will be taken into consideration when formulating the budget this October.
"Based on our initial discussions, as I mentioned earlier, several new pillars and initiatives by the ministry and agricultural programmes will remain a focus, and I believe the allocation should be increased in line with the commendable performance," he said.
He said this in his speech at the closing ceremony of the Malaysia Agriculture, Horticulture and Agrotourism Exhibition (MAHA) 2026 at the Malaysia Agro Exposition Park Serdang (MAEPS) here today.
Also present were Minister of Agriculture and Food Security Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu; Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amiruddin Shari; Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar; and MAFS secretary-general Datuk Seri Isham Ishak.
Anwar said he had no objection to increasing funding for the ministry, given that it would directly benefit farmers, paddy farmers, smallholders and fishermen.
However, the Prime Minister stressed that any increase in the allocation must be accompanied by strict, prudent and integrity-driven governance to prevent any leakage or misappropriation of funds.
Meanwhile, Anwar also praised the success of MAHA 2026, which recorded an outstanding achievement and the highest attendance in its history, demonstrating the people's keen interest in and deep focus on the country's agricultural sector.
He said the success was reflected in the more than 4.3 million visitors recorded at this year's MAHA, with total sales reaching RM66.88 million.
"MAHA 2026, with a strong team this year, has clearly recorded the greatest progress in its history. But what makes it different and has attracted attention is the participation of smallholders, farmers, investors and entrepreneurs from various segments of the agricultural industry, as well as the participation of the people as a whole.
"This means that if we want to develop this country, I do not know whether there is any other exhibition or event that can attract almost five million visitors like this," he said.
The 14th edition of MAHA, held from Aug 28 to today (Sept 6), involved about 2,000 exhibitors and targeted more than four million visitors.
It is the country's main agricultural platform, bringing together industry players, government agencies, entrepreneurs, as well as research and higher education institutions to showcase innovation, technology and business opportunities in the agri-food sector.

Title: Too early to name PM candidate for GE16, says Zahid
Article:
ISKANDAR PUTERI: It is still too early to name a prime ministerial candidate for the 16th General Election (GE16), says Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.
The Umno president said there was no need to discuss the matter yet as the date for Parliament's dissolution and GE16 had not been decided.
"It is too early to put forward someone for the post of prime minister as the election could still be some way off, or it could happen sooner.
"We do not know when Parliament will be dissolved. I think we should set that aside for now and focus on the Melaka election," he said.
The deputy prime minister and rural and regional development minister said this after officiating the closing of the 2026 National Orang Asli Sports Carnival at the EduCity Sports Complex here today.
Zahid said the focus should now be on the Melaka polls before any discussions on federal-level political matters take place.
On political cooperation for the Melaka election, he said this would only be decided after the Melaka Legislative Assembly was dissolved.
Earlier, Pas president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang was reported to have said the party had a potential prime ministerial candidate from among its leaders for GE16, but that it was not yet time to reveal the person.
Hadi said the prime ministerial candidate would only be determined after assessing the strength of the seats won by the parties contesting the election.
He said this at the 72nd Pas Annual Muktamar at the Pusat Tarbiah Islamiah Kelantan (Putik), Pengkalan Chepa, Kota Baru, on Friday.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Former Skudai rep Marina Ibrahim appointed Johor special officer for Orang Asli
Article:
ISKANDAR PUTERI: Former Skudai assemblyman Marina Ibrahim has been appointed Special Officer for the Orang Asli community in Johor under the Sultan Ibrahim Johor Foundation.
The foundation is also known as Yayasan Sultan Ibrahim Johor.
The appointment was announced by Johor Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi, who spoke as a special representative of the Sultan of Johor, Sultan Ibrahim, to engage with and understand the needs of the state's Orang Asli community.
"With the consent of the Yang di-Pertuan Agong, who is also the Sultan of Johor, Sultan Ibrahim, there is now a new special officer, namely Marina Ibrahim.
"Besides that, state Agriculture, Agro-Based Industry and Rural Development committee member Israk Abdullah will also help look after the welfare of the Orang Asli community in the state," he said at the 2026 National Level Orang Asli Sports Carnival at the EduCity Sports Complex here today.
Deputy Prime Minister and Rural and Regional Development Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said he was confident Marina could play an effective role by visiting Orang Asli villages to personally understand the challenges faced by the community.
He said this approach was important to ensure all problems faced by the Orang Asli community were identified and given due attention.
"I am confident Marina will go down to the ground, including to about 60 Orang Asli villages in Johor, to understand the problems they face.
"This will, in turn, improve the development and wellbeing of the Orang Asli community," he said.
Marina, who joined DAP in 2017, served as Skudai assemblyman from March 2022 after winning the seat in the Johor state election with a majority of 13,943 votes.
She announced her decision not to defend the Skudai state seat and
withdrew from politics in May
to refocus on community work.
