Title: Escalating attacks upending daily life in Kyiv
Article:
COMMUTERS, children rushed underground in the middle of the school day, festivals cancelled, walks punctuated by booming air defences.
Near-constant drone attacks are the stark new reality in Kyiv, and daily life is likely to get harder.
Kyiv has survived many traumas since Russia's full-scale invasion in February 2022.
Despite the initial shock of war and the advent of attack drones and ballistic missiles, residents adapted and managed to impose a semblance of normality.
But as a fifth full winter of war approaches, that is becoming harder to maintain.
Over the summer, Moscow began sending swarms of high-speed, jet-propelled drones that are more destructive and harder to shoot down than older propeller-powered models.
For the last 10 days, air attacks have been around-the-clock rather than mainly at night, puncturing Ukrainians' sense that their country's own long-range drone campaign against Russia was swinging the war back in their favour.
Vitaliia Poliakova and her partner were driving near a bridge on the eastern bank of the Dnipro on Thursday when a jet-powered drone struck the road near their car, injuring both.
"We were driving, talking about our own things. Then there was a sudden hit," the 35-year-old said, speaking in the back of an ambulance.
Poliakova had cuts to her right hand and her partner had a bloodied face and right leg.
Foremost in the minds of many of Kyiv's three million residents is the approach of winter.
[[nid:1526852]]
Russian attacks have caused regular power and water outages since early in the war, but their intensity in the last 10 days points to greater disruption.
"The last year has been really difficult for us," said Bohdan, 29, as he surveyed his damaged apartment block, struck in a Russian attack earlier this week.
"After this (attack), as you can see, it will probably be even harder, so we're moving away."
With frontline fighting causing hundreds of casualties a week but yielding little in terms of territorial gains, Russia and Ukraine have engaged in an escalating air war in recent months, hammering each other's energy and logistics facilities.
The UN has verified more than 16,000 civilian deaths so far in the conflict, the vast majority of them in Ukraine.
Both Moscow and Kyiv say they do not target civilians, but in Kyiv and the surrounding region, dozens of civilians have been killed since Aug 27.
On Monday, repeated air raid alerts halted metro services linking the two sides of the Dnipro river that divides the city.
At Osokorky station near the opposite bank to the centre, nurse and psychologist Yulianna Oliynyk and her two sons waited on a packed platform for the alarm to be lifted.
"I'm already thinking maybe we should just take sleeping bags and sleep in the metro at the station near the school," she said. "Last year it was difficult at school and now I honestly don't even know what to do. I just don't know."
Roads into central Kyiv are clogged, bus stops are crammed and people are walking long distances to get to and from work.
[[nid:1526851]]
Grocery shopping is becoming more difficult. Large supermarkets close when air raid sirens sound, meaning customers must leave the building mid-shop.
Natalia Petrivska, executive director at the Ukrainian Food Retail Alliance, appeared on television this week to reassure people that they did not need to panic buy.
Russia fired more than 2,800 jet-powered drones at Ukraine in August.
Ukraine says they are designed to break civilian morale and persuade the government to give up territory.
On the first day of the new academic year this week, pupils at one Kyiv school had just finished their first class when air raid sirens sounded and they hurried to underground shelters to continue their studies.
"It's stressful for them, but the children are becoming better able to adapt," said headmaster Roman Feshchuk.
Around 400 children were enrolled this year at the school, which was damaged in an earlier Russian attack in May, although fewer first-graders had signed up, Feshchuk told Reuters.
Oleksandra, a young girl wearing a traditional Ukrainian dress and carrying flowers to celebrate the new academic year, said she particularly enjoyed arts and crafts.
Asked what she dreamed of, she replied: "That the war will end."
* The writers are from Reuters
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Kedah warns moving Lima could hurt Langkawi's economy
Article:
ALOR STAR: The Kedah government is concerned that moving the Langkawi International Maritime and Aerospace Exhibition (Lima) to another state could affect Langkawi's economy, image and standing as an international tourism destination.
State Tourism, Culture and Entrepreneurship Committee chairman Datuk Mohd Salleh Saidin said Lima had become deeply intertwined with Langkawi after more than three decades of being held on the island.
He said Lima was not merely a defence exhibition but also played a significant role in the local tourism, hospitality, transport, business and economic sectors.
"If the issue is access, then resolve the access problem.
"Don't move an event that has already taken root in Langkawi simply because there is a problem.
"Lima is not just a name or an exhibition. It has become part of Langkawi's identity and generates economic spillover for residents and tourism industry players," he said after the state-level Maulidur Rasul celebration for the Kubang Rotan state constituency here yesterday.
He was commenting on Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin's statement that the government was exploring Melaka as an alternative venue for Lima in future should Langkawi no longer be considered suitable.
Salleh said tourism development in other states could still be pursued through new events or products rather than taking over an event that already had a strong identity at another destination.
He said feedback from industry players and visitors showed that Lima continued to hold significant value for Langkawi.
"The response I received was quite unfavourable towards the proposal.
"Lima is an event eagerly awaited by industry players in Langkawi.
"The last edition recorded the highest number of visitors in Lima's history," he said.
Lima 2025, held in Langkawi in May last year, recorded about 450,000 visitors and brought together 860 exhibitors from 24 countries.
A total of 43 aircraft and 31 ships also took part during the five-day exhibition.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: More money for Agriculture Ministry? Anwar says maybe — if the books stay clean, so farmers won’t suffer
Article:
SERDANG, Sept 6 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today said the Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security could receive a bigger allocation in Budget 2027, provided the ministry continues to uphold good governance.
His remarks came after its minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu called for an additional allocation during the closing ceremony of the Malaysia Agriculture, Horticulture and Agrotourism Exhibition here.
Anwar, who is also finance minister, said additional funding could be considered as long as the ministry ensured that public money was managed properly and reached farmers, fishermen and paddy planters.
“Because large expenditures must be managed well, and we have no choice.
“If we want to safeguard the fate of farmers, paddy planters, and traders, we must ensure good management.
“Allocations may increase, but if there are leakages and misappropriation, those who suffer are the farmers, fishermen, and paddy planters,” he said.
Speaking to reporters later, Mohamad who is better known as Mat Sabu, said the additional allocation is to allow his ministry to prepare early for potential challenges next year.
He said this includes measures to deal with the El Niño phenomenon, which is expected to continue into early next year.
The ministry also needs to be prepared for a possible spike in fertiliser prices amid ongoing geopolitical tensions, he said.
“Our secretary-general has already mapped out our requirements and early measures, particularly if temperatures surge.
“Aquaculture will take a hit. We’re looking at potential fish loss and similar issues. So we must have aid ready to deploy.
“And that’s just one scenario out of many. Say there’s a sudden surge in fertiliser prices; we then need to ask the government for financial support as well,” Mohamad said.
He said the request is essentially for supplementary funds, and that it can be adjusted according to how conditions develop later.
The government will table Budget 2027 when the Dewan Rakyat sits again next month.

Title: FT mufti: ‘Religious exploitation’ more accurate term, not ‘riding on religion’, to describe misuse
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 6 — The term ‘religious exploitation’ is more appropriate and objective than ‘riding on religion’ to describe the act of misusing religion for worldly interests, said Federal Territories Mufti Ahmad Fauwaz Fadzil.
He said the term ‘riding on religion’ should not be used indiscriminately as it could lead to generalisations about religious figures, including scholars and preachers who sincerely champion the cause of Islam.
The term ‘religious exploitation’ focuses more specifically on the act of misusing religion to gain wealth, influence or position, while also more clearly illustrating the existence of those who take advantage and those who are deceived.
“On the other hand, the term ‘riding’ has a negative and harsh connotation and tends to carry elements of sarcasm and personal accusations against the perpetrator.
“The term ‘religious exploitation’ more accurately describes the power structure in this phenomenon, namely the existence of those who take advantage (exploit) and those who are exploited (members of the public who are deceived or misled), in line with the actual meaning of the evidence from the Quran and Sunnah,” he said in the Tinta Mufti column published by the Federal Territories Mufti Department today.
Ahmad Fauwaz said the exploitation of religion was prohibited and condemned in the Quran, including through verses in Surah At-Taubah and Surah Al-Baqarah, both of which illustrate forms of religious exploitation that occur when religion is manipulated as a tool to obtain wealth and worldly interests, an act that is reprehensible as it exploits the name of Allah for personal gain.
He said the Prophet Muhammad also warned against those who use religion to deceive people for worldly interests, as narrated by al-Tirmidhi, which means: “At the end of time, a group of men will emerge who deceive people by using religion to obtain worldly gains... their tongues are sweeter than sweets, while their hearts are the hearts of wolves.”
Ahmad Fauwaz said the hadith described individuals who present themselves as knowledgeable and pious to gain the trust of the community, while using religion as a guise to obtain money, influence or position.
In this regard, he advised the public not to be easily deceived by outward appearances, but instead to conduct proper checks before placing their trust, wealth or obedience in any individual who uses religion as a tool for personal gain.
At the same time, he reminded those involved in preaching, religious knowledge and religious work to always maintain sincerity and fulfil their responsibilities solely for the sake of Allah and to attain His pleasure. — Bernama

Title: Kedah appeals for continued cloud seeding as Pedu, Muda and Ahning dam levels keep falling
Article:
ALOR SETAR, Sept 6 — The Kedah state government appealed for the continuation of cloud seeding operations, coordinated by the National Disaster Management Agency (NADMA), to help raise declining water levels at dams in the state.
State Public Works, Natural Resources, Water Supply, Water Resources and Environment Committee chairman Datuk Mohamad Yusoff Zakaria said that while the operation carried out from Thursday to yesterday resulted in rain, it was still insufficient to boost reservoir levels.
He said before cloud seeding on Sept 2, total water supply at the Pedu, Muda and Ahning Dams stood at 37.14 per cent, but had dropped to 36.64 per cent this morning.
“The water level at Pedu Dam is now at 38.46 per cent, compared to 39.02 per cent on Sept 2, while Muda Dam recorded 9.04 per cent, down from 9.32 per cent previously,” he told Bernama today.
Meanwhile, supply at Ahning Dam stood at 45.00 per cent, compared to 45.32 per cent over the same period.
He said sufficient dam water supply is critical to ensure the smooth operation of padi irrigation systems, as Kedah’s agricultural sector is heavily dependent on these water sources.
Earlier, the federal government took early and targeted measures to address dry weather conditions, low rainfall, and the risk of deteriorating air quality through cloud seeding operations in Kedah and Perlis. — Bernama

Title: Bukit Lagi Hindu temple row: Perlis police get two more days to detain activist as probe widens into criminal trespass
Article:
KANGAR, Sept 6 — The remand of a 55-year-old activist detained over social media posts linked to a gathering concerning the demolition of a Hindu temple in Bukit Lagi has been extended by two days as police pursue a separate criminal trespass investigation.
Magistrate Ana Rozana Mohd Nor allowed the police application today for the extension, with the activist being investigated under Section 447 of the Penal Code, Harian Metro reported today.
Kangar district police chief Assistant Commissioner Yusharifuddin Mohd Yusop confirmed with the Malay newspaper that the suspect would remain in custody until tomorrow to assist investigations into the alleged criminal trespass.
The activist was initially remanded for two days from September 5 to assist investigations into allegedly inciting social media posts related to the organisation of a gathering over the demolition of the Sri Veera Maha Kaliamman Kovil temple in Bukit Lagi.
He was arrested in Petaling Jaya, Selangor last Thursday following 15 police reports lodged between August 22 and 27 over posts made through his TikTok account.
The earlier investigation is being conducted under Section 4(1) of the Sedition Act 1948 and Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998.
Police had said the posts included a picture promoting the Perhimpunan Merah Maha Kali gathering, which was held at the temple site on August 30.
The temple was demolished by the authorities on August 20, with police previously saying the gathering was believed to have been organised in response to dissatisfaction over the demolition.
Police had also warned that the gathering could potentially trigger racial and religious tensions in Perlis.

Title: Fadhlina pledges no SJKT closures as RM12.6m Sungai Bakap Tamil school project gets going after 17 years
Article:
NIBONG TEBAL, Sept 6 — The government has assured that no Tamil vernacular school will be closed as construction finally begins on a RM12.6 million replacement building for SJKT Sungai Bakap after nearly 17 years of delays.
Education Minister Fadhlina Sidek said the Madani Government would instead continue to focus on the development and maintenance of all SJKT, as well as programmes to strengthen teachers and pupils.
She said the assurance was necessary as there were still perceptions in the community that some SJKT could be shut down.
“We give an assurance that, under the Madani Government, no SJKT will be closed.
“Instead, we will focus on all schools in terms of development, maintenance and programmes related to strengthening teachers and pupils,” she said.
Fadhlina was speaking to reporters after witnessing the groundbreaking and handover of the letter of acceptance for the new SJKT Sungai Bakap building here today.
The RM12.6 million project, to be carried out by Yayasan Didik Negara and monitored by the Penang Education Department, is expected to be completed within 56 weeks.
The new school will be built at a site about 2km from the existing location and will comprise six classrooms, special-purpose rooms and other facilities.
Fadhlina, who is also Nibong Tebal MP, said the new building was important in providing better and more comprehensive educational facilities for children in the Sungai Bakap area.
She also apologised to parents, pupils and teachers for the long wait before the project could finally be realised.
The project had been delayed since 2009 due to implementation issues, financial constraints and legal disputes, according to Bernama.
Penang special committee chairman for Tamil schools Datuk Seri S. Sundarajoo said the existing school building, which houses more than 100 pupils, was in a dilapidated condition.
He said the project had previously faced issues involving land, contractor delays and court proceedings before these were resolved.
Sundarajoo, who is also the state housing and environment executive councillor, said the state government was targeting the construction of three SJKT buildings this year.
He said SJKT Sungai Bakap was the second to be developed, while work on SJKT Juru was expected to begin before the end of the year.

Title: Volcanic ash grounds 20 Malaysia-Jakarta flights by Malaysia Airlines, Batik Air
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 6 — Malaysia Airlines and Batik Air have cancelled a total of 20 flights between Malaysia and Jakarta today after volcanic ash from the ongoing eruption of Mount Anak Krakatau disrupted operations at Jakarta’s Soekarno-Hatta International Airport (CGK).
Malaysia Airlines said in its post on X that it would cancel 12 flights between Kuala Lumpur (KUL) and Jakarta (CGK), namely MH713, MH712, MH711, MH710, MH717, MH716, MH721, MH720, MH723, MH722, MH725 and MH724.
“Given the evolving situation, Malaysia Airlines is closely monitoring developments.
“Further updates on affected flights will be communicated directly to affected customers,” it said.
The national carrier reminded passengers to ensure their contact details are up to date via “My Booking” on its website to receive timely updates by email and SMS.
Customers may also contact its Live Chat support on the Malaysia Airlines website or its Global Contact Centre for assistance.
“The safety of our passengers and crew remains our utmost priority,” it added.
Meanwhile, Batik Air said in a separate statement that it had cancelled eight scheduled flights between Malaysia and Jakarta today, namely OD398, OD399, OD346, OD347, OD388, OD389, OD390 and OD391.
Six of the cancelled services operate between Kuala Lumpur International Airport and Jakarta, while two operate between Subang and Jakarta.
It said the decision followed close coordination with aviation authorities and airport operators, reflecting its commitment to the safety and wellbeing of passengers and crew.
“The presence of volcanic ash in the airspace can reduce visibility, interfere with aircraft navigation systems, and potentially compromise engine performance,” it said.
Batik Air said it would continue to monitor the situation and provide updates on flight operations to and from the affected destinations through its official website and social media channels.
Affected passengers would also be notified through their registered contact details.
“Affected passengers may request to reschedule their travel to the next available Batik Air flight, subject to availability, or request a refund.
“Passengers are advised to contact Batik Air’s Customer Care Centre or their respective booking channels for assistance with their preferred option,” it said.
Batik Air, a Malaysian carrier, operates under Indonesia’s Lion Air Group. — Bernama

Title: United Sikhs Malaysia head into Nepal’s worst-hit flood zone to help 98 kids whose parents are missing (VIDEO)
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 6 — Five Malaysian volunteers are heading deep into one of Nepal’s worst-hit flood zones, travelling over rough terrain to deliver emergency supplies and help families whose homes and communities have been devastated by floods and landslides.
The team from United Sikhs Malaysia, a Malaysian humanitarian aid organisation involved in disaster relief and community assistance, is travelling to Dhunche in Rasuwa district to establish a base camp before pushing on to Syapru Besi near the Nepal-Tibet border.
In a Facebook post today, the group said that the journey to Dhunche is expected to take 10 to 12 hours, with the team then facing challenging off-road conditions to reach Syapru Besi, about 40km from the border.
The volunteers will first unload relief supplies at their base before continuing to the affected town.
The team’s immediate priority is to build temporary shelters for families displaced by the disaster, the group’s legal director Raspreet Kaur told the
The New Straits Times
.
She said a local resident had also sought help for 98 children whose parents remained missing, with the team planning to provide necessities including colouring materials.
The volunteers had earlier prepared mosquito nets and tarpaulins worth about RM28,000 for around 300 affected families, with the supplies delivered to a gurdwara in Kathmandu.
United Sikhs Malaysia said Team A is expected to remain in Nepal for about two weeks, while additional teams are on standby depending on the situation on the ground.
https://www.facebook.com/UNITEDSIKHSMALAYSIA/videos/06092026-mission-update-nepal-flood-reliefunited-sikhs-malaysias-team-a-is-curre/3827014714104717/
United Sikhs Malaysia’s mission comes as other Malaysian teams and organisations are also responding to the disaster.
Mercy Malaysia has deployed a humanitarian assessment team to Nepal to assess conditions on the ground and identify urgent needs, including emergency shelter, food, clean water, sanitation and healthcare.
Malaysia has also sent 11 officers and personnel from the Special Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (SMART) to assist with search-and-rescue operations in areas affected by the floods and landslides.
The 10-day SMART mission is expected to include operations in areas where people may still be trapped, while the team will also assist in efforts to locate Malaysians affected by the disaster.
The Malaysian government has also pledged US$1 million (RM4.2 million) to help Nepal’s disaster victims and support recovery efforts.
The disaster has particularly disrupted access to communities in Rasuwa, where flooding and landslides have damaged roads, bridges and other infrastructure, making relief operations difficult.

Title: Zahid tells parties to park PM talk, focus on Melaka polls instead
Article:
ISKANDAR PUTERI, Sept 6 — Barisan Nasional chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi today urged political parties to put talk of who could become prime minister after the 16th general election aside for now, saying the focus should instead be on the upcoming Melaka state election.
The Umno president said it was too early to name or discuss a potential prime ministerial candidate when the timing of Parliament’s dissolution and the next general election remained unknown,
Harian Metro
reported.
“It is too early to put forward someone or a particular figure to hold that position because the election could still be far away or it could be otherwise.
“We do not know when Parliament will be dissolved. I think it is better that we put that aside for now and focus on facing the Melaka state election,” he was quoted as saying after the closing of the 2026 National Orang Asli Sports Carnival at the EduCity Sports Complex here.
Zahid, who is also deputy prime minister, said attention should remain on the Melaka election before any discussions on federal-level political matters take place.
On cooperation among political parties for the Melaka election, he said this would only be decided after the Melaka Legislative Assembly was dissolved.
His remarks came after PAS president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang said the party had a potential prime ministerial candidate from among its leaders for GE16, but that it was not yet time to reveal the individual.
He made the remarks at  PAS’ annual congress in Kota Bharu, Kelantan last Friday.

Title: Sarawak extends cloud‑seeding operations to tackle transboundary haze as Serian API shows improving trend
Article:
KUCHING, Sept 6 — Cloud seeding operations across Sarawak have been extended until tomorrow in an ongoing effort to mitigate transboundary haze affecting the state.
Sarawak Disaster Management Committee (SDMC) chairman Datuk Amar Douglas Uggah Embas said the extension followed a successful operation yesterday, which brought rainfall over the targeted Bakun and Murum Dam areas.
“Today’s operation will continue as planned and will be carried out where suitable cloud and weather conditions permit,” he said in a statement today.
Sarawak has been conducting cloud-seeding operations targeting key dams and water catchment areas in the state since Thursday.
Meanwhile, Uggah said air quality in the Serian district had shown an improving trend, with the Air Pollutant Index (API) reading at 185 as at noon today, placing it in the unhealthy category.
“There is a downward trend for the API level in Serian as we enter the second of three days of monitoring. The API is primarily affected by wind direction and the source of hotspots,” he said.
He said continued monitoring was necessary before any formal recommendation regarding Serian’s emergency status could be submitted to Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg and Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
Uggah said data from the Asean Specialised Meteorological Centre (ASMC) revealed zero hotspots in Sarawak, while 184 hotspots were detected in neighbouring Kalimantan, Indonesia. — Bernama

Title: Chief Justice leads 128‑strong Terengganu honours list in conjunction with Sultan Mizan’s 64th birthday
Article:
KUALA TERENGGANU, Sept 6 — Chief Justice Tun Wan Ahmad Farid Wan Salleh topped the list of 128 recipients of the Terengganu state honours and medals in conjunction with the 64th birthday celebration of the Sultan of Terengganu, Sultan Mizan Zainal Abidin.
The Regent of Terengganu, Tengku Muhammad Ismail Sultan Mizan Zainal Abidin, graced the investiture ceremony held at the Balairong Seri of Istana Syarqiyyah here.
Also in attendance were his younger siblings, Tengku Seri Setia Mahkota Raja Tengku Datuk Seri Muhammad Muaz; Tengku Puteri Utama Raja Tengku Nadhirah Zahrah; and Tengku Puteri Daulath Raja Tengku Fatimatuz Zahra’.
Also present were Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar and members of the state government leadership.
Wan Ahmad Farid was conferred the Darjah Kebesaran Seri Setia Sultan Mizan Zainal Abidin Terengganu (S.S.M.Z), which carries the title Datuk Seri.
Also receiving the S.S.M.Z were Qatar Ambassador to Malaysia Datuk Seri Salah Mohammed Al-Sorour; Chief of Air Force General Tan Sri Muhamad Norazlan Aris; and Terengganu Equestrian Association deputy president Tan Sri Abdullah Taib.
Tengku Muhammad Ismail also conferred the Darjah Kebesaran Datuk Setia Sultan Mizan Abidin Terengganu (D.S.M.Z), which carries the title Datuk, on Federal Court Judge Datuk Che Mohd Ruzima Ghazali and CelcomDigi Berhad board adviser and former chief executive officer Datuk Mohamad Idham Nawawi.
Also receiving the D.S.M.Z were executive chairman of Mirmas Holding Sdn Bhd, Datuk Awalan Abdul Aziz and managing partner of Messrs Feroz@Co Datuk Feroz A S Moidunny.
In addition, 27 recipients were conferred the Darjah Kebesaran Datuk Paduka Mahkota Terengganu (D.PMT), which also carries the title Datuk, including renowned actor Datuk Abdul Manan Embong, better known as Eman Manan, and Terengganu Tourism, Culture, Environment and Climate Change Committee chairman Datuk Razali Idris.
Also receiving the same award were Dungun Member of Parliament Datuk Wan Hassan Mohd Ramli; Universiti Malaysia Terengganu vice-chancellor Prof Datuk Dr Mohd Zamri Ibrahim; and Terengganu police chief Datuk Mohd Khairi Khairudin.
Tengku Muhammad Ismail also conferred the Darjah Kebesaran Setia Sultan Mizan Zainal Abidin Terengganu (S.M.Z) on 17 recipients, including Terengganu Information, Dakwah and Syariah Empowerment Committee chairman Muhammad Khalil Abdul Hadi.
At the ceremony, 17 recipients were awarded the Darjah Kebesaran Setia Mahkota Terengganu; 20 received the Darjah Kebesaran Ahli Sultan Mizan Zainal Abidin Terengganu; and 39 individuals were awarded the Darjah Kebesaran Ahli Mahkota Terengganu. — Bernama

Title: Two foreigners remanded for allegedly taking plant specimens without permission from Santubong National Park
Article:
KUCHING, Sept 6 — Two foreign nationals have been remanded for allegedly taking plant specimens without permission from Santubong National Park last Thursday.
Sarawak Forestry Corporation (SFC) said both individuals were remanded for three days, from September 4 to September 7, to assist with the investigation.
“On September 3 at around 1.50pm, the two individuals were checking out of the park after conducting an activity in the area. Following observations, they were suspected of taking and collecting plant specimens from the area.
“Inspections revealed four transparent plastic bags filled with plant specimens, believed to have been taken from the national park. Two backpacks and other items were also seized for further investigation,” SFC said in a statement
All specimens have been recorded and retained as case exhibits, and are currently undergoing identification and further examination to determine their type and species status.
SFC is working with the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) to complete the investigation and any subsequent action.
The investigation also takes into account the provisions under the National Parks & Nature Reserves Ordinance, 1998 [Cap. 27], which prohibits the taking or removal of plants from national park areas without permission from the controller of national parks and nature reserves.
Under Section 26 of the said Ordinance, no person is allowed to take or destroy plants within a national park, or to remove any plant, whether living or dead, without the controller’s permission
“SFC takes a serious view of any activity involving the taking, collecting, or removal of biological resources from Totally Protected Areas (TPAs) without permission. Such activities may impact the integrity of biodiversity and the long-term conservation efforts of Sarawak.
“Members of the public and visitors are reminded that all flora, fauna, and natural resources within national park areas are protected and must not be taken, removed, or carried out without valid authorisation,” SFC said. — The Borneo Post

Title: Former minister’s remand extended two days in Tabung Haji RCI hotel‑lease probe
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 6 — The remand of a former minister detained over investigations into a Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) hotel‑lease issue in Saudi Arabia has been extended for two more days.
According to Bernama, Magistrate Muhammad Bukhori Md Ruslan Zakariah issued the extension, which runs from tomorrow until Tuesday, after the Malaysian Anti‑Corruption Commission (MACC) applied for it at the Putrajaya Magistrate’s Court this morning.
MACC Chief Commissioner Abd Halim Aman, when contacted, said the case is being investigated under Section 16(a)(A) of the MACC Act 2009.
The former minister was previously remanded for five days after being detained when he arrived to give a statement to MACC last Wednesday.
The Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on TH, released publicly on July 29, recorded weaknesses in TH’s management and operations between 2014 and 2020 and listed problematic investments requiring forensic audit.
The report also stated that suspicious transactions and concealment of information had occurred.

Title: Anwar expresses solidarity with Indonesia over volcanic disaster and haze challenges
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 6 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today expressed solidarity with the people of Indonesia following the volcanic disaster and haze-related challenges currently facing the country.
Anwar said he conveyed this when he contacted former Indonesian President Joko Widodo, better known as Jokowi, who is currently in Penang to attend the Penang Peace Dialogue.
In a post on his Facebook page today, Anwar said the conversation also saw the two leaders exchange updates.
Anwar also apologised for being unable to meet Jokowi in person in Penang due to his previously scheduled programme with farmers, livestock breeders, smallholders and the agro community at the Malaysia Agriculture, Horticulture and Agrotourism Exhibition (MAHA) 2026.
“Malaysia and Indonesia are not merely neighbouring countries, but two kindred nations bound by history, culture and close ties of brotherhood.
“Positions and responsibilities may change hands, but friendship and mutual respect will endure,” he said, stressing that the ties would continue to be nurtured for the well-being of the people of both countries and the prosperity of the region.
According to a report by national news agency ANTARA, Jokowi attended the Penang Peace Dialogue held in George Town and shared his views on the role of leaders and the people in laying the foundations for peace at a gala dinner last night.
Jokowi is also scheduled to deliver a keynote address at the forum today. — Bernama

Title: DOE monitors bush and peatland fires in Mukah, Daro in Sarawak amid dry spell
Article:
KUCHING, Sept 6 — The Department of Environment (DoE) is paying special attention to the fire incidents reported in bushes and peatlands near Jalan Sibujaya Barat in Mukah and Sungai Nai in Daro amid the current dry spell.
DoE deputy director-general (Development) Azuri Azizah Saedon said based on the latest status, the fire in the Jalan Sibujaya Barat area had been mostly controlled, covering an area of nine hectares.
“However, the fire still affects approximately one hectare in the Jalan Sibujaya Barat area and is currently being extinguished,” she said in a statement on Sunday.
In Sungai Nai, Azuri said approximately 2.5 of the three hectares are still burning, but the situation is reported to be under control, according to the Fire and Rescue Services Department.
She said fires in vegetation and peatland have the potential to produce smoke and release pollutants that can affect local air quality if left unchecked.
As such, she said the DoE Sarawak will continue monitoring the latest status of the fires at the mentioned locations, including assessing the potential impact on air quality.
Drone flights will also be carried out to obtain the latest picture of the fire status and the extent of the affected area, she added.
“Air quality monitoring and follow-up actions will be carried out based on the actual situation on the ground and the results of the DoE assessment together with relevant agencies.”
Azuri said monitoring would be strengthened if there was an increase in air pollution, while appropriate actions would be taken in accordance with the existing legal provisions to minimise the impact of the fire on the environment and public health.
In the meantime, she reminded members of the public that open burning is an offence under the Environmental Quality (Amendment) Act 2024, which carries a fine ranging from RM25,000 to RM1,000,000, or imprisonment of up to five years, or both.
She said a compound of up to 50 per cent of the maximum fine may also be imposed for each offence.
Everyone is urged to report any fire or open burning to the Fire and Rescue Department at 999 or the DoE at 1-800-88-2727.
Meanwhile, Azuri said two air quality monitoring stations in Sarawak recorded very unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 10am on Sunday. They were Kuching with an API of 223 and Sri Aman (215).
Ten of the 35 locations across the country that registered unhealthy API readings were in Sarawak. They were Samalaju (200), Bintulu (198), Mukah (194), Samarahan (192), Sarikei (188), Serian and Industrial Training Institute Miri (both 182), Sibu (181), Miri (175) and Limbang (160).
The remaining air quality monitoring stations with unhealthy API were Selangor (6), Johor (4), Sabah and Negeri Sembilan (3 each), Kuala Lumpur, Melaka and Pahang (2 each), Putrajaya, Terengganu and Labuan (1 each).
Based on the Asean Specialised Meteorological Centre (ASMC) report on Saturday, Azuri said a total of 184 hotspots were detected in Kalimantan, 373 in Sumatra and one in Perak.
“ASMC also reported moderate to thick transboundary smoke plumes observed covering the northern part of Borneo.
“Moderate to thick smoke plumes were also observed from hotspots detected in many areas of Kalimantan as well as central and southern Sumatra,” she said.
She added that moderate haze was also observed in Singapore and southern Peninsular Malaysia. — The Borneo Post

Title: After quitting politics, former Skudai rep Marina Ibrahim is now Johor Sultan’s special officer for Orang Asli affairs
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Sept 6 — Marina Ibrahim, who recently stepped away from politics, is taking on a new role representing the Sultan of Johor in engaging with the state’s Orang Asli community.
The former Skudai assemblyman from DAP has been appointed a special officer for Orang Asli affairs under the Sultan Ibrahim Johor Foundation, news outlet
Free Malaysia Today
reported.
Johor Menteri Besar Onn Hafiz Ghazi made the announcement yesterday, saying Marina will work with the community to better understand its needs, while state Agriculture, Agro-based Industry and Rural Development executive councillor Israk Abdullah would also oversee Orang Asli welfare.
Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said he was confident Marina could contribute effectively by visiting Orang Asli villages and gaining firsthand understanding of the issues faced by the community.
Zahid said such an approach was important to ensure the community’s problems were identified and given due attention.
Marina announced on May 31 that she would not defend Skudai in the July 11 state election and would leave politics to continue her social work.
Johor DAP chairman Teo Nie Ching later said the party had planned to move Marina to contest Tiram.
Marina won Skudai in the 2022 Johor election, defeating Barisan Nasional’s Lim Soon Hai and Perikatan Nasional’s Khoo Keng Ek.

Title: Zahid denies rift with Anwar, reaffirms BN’s commitment to political stability
Article:
ISKANDAR PUTERI, Sept 6 — Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has denied claims of a rift or problems between him and Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, stressing instead that Barisan Nasional (BN) remains committed to ensuring the country’s political stability until the end of the term.
He said there were no problems, either personally or in official capacity, between him and Anwar, including when attending Cabinet meetings as well as official government functions and events.
“I have no problems, either personally or in an official capacity. What is important for Barisan Nasional (BN), as one of the components of the Unity Government, is political stability in the country until the end of the term.
“We make and reach decisions professionally,” he told reporters after attending the national-level Orang Asli Sports Carnival at the Educity Sports Complex here today.
Also present was Johor Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi.
He said this when asked to comment on a Bloomberg report which previously said that relations between him and Anwar were reportedly becoming increasingly strained, resulting in recent Cabinet meetings being shorter than usual.
The report said the tension stemmed from Ahmad Zahid’s decision for BN to oppose Pakatan Harapan (PH) in the recent Johor and Negeri Sembilan state elections.
The BN chairman also said the coalition’s commitment to remain in the Unity Government until the end of its term was in line with the resolution of the Umno General Assembly.
He said political stability was crucial to ensuring continued foreign investor confidence in Malaysia while supporting the country’s economic growth.
“We know that the resolution of the Umno General Assembly has stipulated that we remain in the Unity Government until the end of its term.
“This is what we are doing to ensure full political stability and avoid any problems, particularly involving foreign investors, foreign direct investment, as well as to boost the country’s economic growth,” he said.
He said claims of problems between the BN leadership and the Prime Minister did not reflect the actual situation.
“The fact is that there are no problems when we are in Cabinet meetings or at official functions or events of ministries, departments and agencies at the federal level,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Anwar: MACC to investigate fertiliser‑supply delay to paddy farmers in Kedah; errant contractors may face termination
Article:
SERDANG, Sept 6 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has instructed the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) to investigate the issue of delays in the supply of Fertiliser 3 to paddy farmers in the Muda Agricultural Development Authority (MADA) area in Kedah.
He stressed that the delays should not have occurred and must not be allowed to recur.
Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, said that if any wrongdoing was detected, action should be taken to terminate the supply contract, including prosecution in accordance with the country’s laws against those responsible or any companies involved.
“Which company was entrusted with the responsibility? Did they fulfil their promise or not? If they did not fulfil it, why was no action taken against them? If a company like this repeatedly makes mistakes, terminate the contract! Appoint a new company.
“Do not make farmers and paddy farmers the victims. Take action; if there has been wrongdoing, bring them to court. If they are to be charged, let MACC come in and review this process,” he said in his speech at the closing ceremony of the Malaysia Agriculture, Horticulture and Agrotourism Exhibition (MAHA) 2026 here today.
Anwar said paddy farmers should not be burdened with any issues that disrupt their livelihoods, especially at a time when they are already facing other problems, including water supply and hot weather conditions.
He said the issue of delays in the fertiliser supply had also directly tarnished the image of the Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security (MAFS).
“MAFS has a clean record under Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu. Its officials and ministry staff have always been committed to helping paddy farmers, but the damage caused has given the government a bad image.
“So, I want to use this opportunity to say that the government will do whatever possible to continue uplifting and helping paddy farmers, and those in the agriculture and livestock sectors,” he said.
The media had previously reported a call by Pengkalan Kundor assemblywoman Mardhiyyah Johari for the government to consider compensation for paddy farmers who suffered losses due to delays in the distribution of Additional Compound Fertiliser, or Paddy Fertiliser 3, in the MADA area.
The delay was reported to have affected about 38,000 paddy farmers cultivating 78,117 hectares of paddy in the MADA area.
Mohamad Sabu, in a statement, said the Paddy Fertiliser 3 had been supplied to MADA paddy farmers since last Thursday and was expected to be fully distributed within 10 days. — Bernama

Title: TV volume row leaves woman with slash wound in Kota Tinggi, cops nab husband
Article:
KOTA TINGGI, Sept 6 — Police have arrested a Malaysian man in his 70s after he allegedly slashed his wife with a
parang
during an argument over the TV volume at their house in Taman Desa Sejahtera here.
Kota Tinggi police received information at about 9.30pm yesterday about an injured woman bleeding from the wound at home, district police chief Superintendent Yusof Othman said in a Facebook statement today.
He said a police team was sent to the house where they found the man, who is the victim’s husband, and arrested him.
Early investigation found that the couple quarrelled after the wife increased the television volume before the suspect, who was reportedly intoxicated, allegedly attacked her with the blade.
The woman, also in her 70s, suffered a 1cm slash wound to her right arm and was taken to Kota Tinggi Hospital, where she is now in a stable condition.
Police seized the weapon and are investigating the case under Section 324 of the Penal Code for voluntarily causing hurt with a dangerous weapon or means.

Title: Anthony Loke says govt has 15 months to finish reforms, no need to rush GE16
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 6 — DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke today said there is no need to rush into the 16th general election, with the unity government still having 15 months to complete its reform agenda.
His remarks came amid calls from several quarters for Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim to dissolve Parliament early and pave the way for GE16, including from Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.
“Following the recent state elections in Johor and Melaka, we have heard a great deal of news and voices from various parties and quarters pressuring the prime minister to dissolve Parliament and pave the way for the 16th general election,” he was quoted by The Star as saying at the Wanita DAP national congress here.
Loke said DAP’s position was that Anwar should not give in to such pressure as long as he retained majority support in the Dewan Rakyat.
“We have the remaining 15 months to complete the reforms,” he added.
He said the unity government was formed following the 15th general election in 2022 and should be allowed to use the remainder of its current term to deliver on its commitments.
Anwar has said the proposal for an earlier election could be considered, but that the government was currently focused on reviving the economy, improving public well-being and fighting corruption and abuse of power.
Loke said political differences between parties in the unity government did not mean they were no longer able to govern together.
“As long as every party still sticks to the government, then in terms of governance, we should be able to govern the country,” he said.
He said DAP had yet to decide whether to work with BN in the Melaka state election, adding that it was not involved in negotiations between Pakatan Harapan election director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari and Melaka BN chairman Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh.
Loke, who is also the transport minister, said DAP remains focused on reforms already agreed upon by the Cabinet, including constitutional amendments involving the separation of the attorney general and public prosecutor roles and a proposed term limit for the prime minister.

Title: KLIA sets up resting areas for Jakarta‑bound passengers after Anak Krakatau ash forces airport shutdown
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 6 — Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) has urged passengers bound for Jakarta on affected flights to contact their airlines for the latest schedule information, after volcanic ash from Anak Krakatau forced the temporary closure of Soekarno-Hatta International Airport.
In a travel advisory, KLIA confirmed the ash-related closure and added via social media that resting areas have been set up for affected passengers awaiting further news.
“At Terminal 1, the designated resting areas are at Anjung Tinjau, Level 5 of the Main Terminal Building; the CRS Area, Level 3 of the Main Terminal Building; and Gate C36, Mezzanine Level of the Satellite Building.
“At Terminal 2, the resting area is located at Level 3A (Mezzanine Floor), Departure Hall,” it said.
Anak Krakatau, situated in the Sunda Strait between Java and Sumatra, continued its eruption on Saturday, with authorities reporting lava-fountaining activity and audible booming and rumbling sounds from an observation post.
The eruption began at 11.07 pm local time on Friday and persisted throughout observations from midnight to 6 am on Saturday.
Indonesia’s Centre for Volcanology and Geological Hazard Mitigation said the volcano remains at Level III, or Siaga (Alert), with a three-kilometre exclusion zone in place around its active crater.
Authorities added that the volcano’s regrown edifice is relatively small and is not considered capable of collapsing on a scale that could generate a tsunami. — Bernama

Title: DPM Zahid: Over 600 Orang Asli students now pursuing higher education, reflecting rising social mobility
Article:
ISKANDAR PUTERI, Sept 6 — More than 600 Orang Asli children are now pursuing their studies at universities and colleges nationwide, reflecting a significant increase in the community’s participation in higher education and demonstrating the government’s concern for the group’s education.
Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the achievement was among the outcomes of the government’s emphasis on education as an important instrument to improve the social mobility of the Orang Asli community.
The Rural and Regional Development Minister said that when the Department of Orang Asli Development (JAKOA) was placed under his ministry four years ago, an initial target was set for 200 Orang Asli children to gain admission to higher education institutions.
“In the first year, the challenge was accepted. Not only did 200 enter university, but the number exceeded 300 Orang Asli who entered university that year.
“In the second year, I increased the target to 300. Clearly, the achievement of Orang Asli children entering university increased to 400 in the second year,” he said in his speech at the national-level Orang Asli Sports Carnival (KSOA) at EduCity Sports Complex here today.
Also present was Johor Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi.
Ahmad Zahid said the achievement of more than 600 students this year proved that the Orang Asli community had the ability to progress if given the appropriate educational opportunities and support.
“This represents good social mobility because education is an element that can improve the social status of any community in the world,” he said.
He said efforts to empower education among the Orang Asli community had also been expanded to Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) through the provision of institutions specifically for the community.
Among them is the Paya Bungor Training Centre in Maran, Pahang, which currently has 135 Orang Asli students enrolled in TVET programmes offering both short- and long-term courses.
Meanwhile, Ahmad Zahid also expressed his appreciation for the Johor government’s commitment in allocating RM600,000 to 60 Orang Asli villages in the state, amounting to RM10,000 for each village.
He also expressed hope that the allocation could be increased in the Johor Budget for next year.
Ahmad Zahid also expressed his appreciation to His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, for appointing former Skudai assemblywoman Marina Ibrahim as special officer in charge of Orang Asli affairs under the Sultan Ibrahim Foundation.
He said the appointment reflected His Majesty’s concern for the welfare and development of the Orang Asli community in Johor. — Bernama

Title: PM term limit, AG-PP split: DAP wants both Bills tabled in Oct-Dec sitting
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 6 — DAP is pushing for two constitutional reform Bills covering the prime minister’s tenure and the separation of the attorney general and public prosecutor to be brought back to the Dewan Rakyat when its next sitting begins on October 5.
DAP chairman Gobind Singh Deo said both draft Bills were ready and should be tabled during the sitting, which runs until December 8.
“The matter has been discussed and the drafts are ready. I have asked for both Bills to be tabled,” he was quoted by
The New Straits Times
as saying today.
According to Gobind, de facto Law and Institutional Reform Minister Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said that the Bills were ready as part of the government’s institutional reform agenda.
The proposed prime ministerial term-limit amendment would cap a person’s tenure as prime minister at 10 years.
The measure narrowly failed to secure the required two-thirds majority in the Dewan Rakyat in March, receiving 146 votes in favour — two short of the 148 needed.
Following the defeat, Deputy Prime Minister II Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof said the government was confident of securing sufficient support when the Bill was retabled and that government MPs would support it.
Azalina said on September 3 that the Bill was now ready for its second reading, although its tabling and voting would be subject to the decision of Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim as leader of the House.
She also said the constitutional amendments would require a two-thirds majority.
Gobind said the term-limit proposal should be refined before its second reading.
The other reform would separate the attorney general’s role as the government’s legal adviser from that of the public prosecutor, who oversees criminal prosecutions.
The proposed separation was referred to a parliamentary special select committee for further scrutiny after being tabled earlier this year, with the draft subsequently revised.
Azalina said the revised proposal was also ready for Parliament and that the changes included a greater role for Parliament in scrutinising the appointment of the public prosecutor.
Gobind also said DAP had also raised the vacant attorney general’s post and equal allocations for elected representatives at its central executive committee meeting, with both matters to be brought to the central Pakatan Harapan leadership.
“We hope the appointment process can be completed as soon as possible, including taking into account the views of the public and opposition MPs,” he was quoted as saying.
He said the appointment of the attorney general and public prosecutor should be free from political discrimination.
“We respect the mandate given to every elected representative,” he added.

Title: AirAsia cancels, reschedules Jakarta flights as Anak Krakatau erupts
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 6 — A number of AirAsia flights to and from Jakarta have been cancelled or rescheduled following the continued eruption of Mount Anak Krakatau in Indonesia’s Sunda Strait, which has generated extensive volcanic ash clouds.
In a statement today, AirAsia said volcanic ash posed a significant threat to aircraft safety, prompting operational adjustments to selected services whose flight paths may be affected.
“AirAsia has notified all affected guests on their flight status and recovery options,” the airline said, adding that it was working to ensure passengers could resume their journeys safely on the next available flight.
The situation remains fluid, and AirAsia urged passengers travelling to and from the affected destinations to check their latest flight status before travelling.
“AirAsia is continuing to monitor Mount Anak Krakatau’s volcanic activity and will update its travel advisory with the resumption of normal operations,” it added.
Passengers can check their latest flight status via AirAsia’s website or contact its customer support team for further assistance. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia’s SMART team begins Nepal mission after arriving in Kathmandu
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 6 — The Special Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (SMART) MAS01, which was deployed on a Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief (HADR) mission to Nepal, safely arrived at Tribhuvan International Airport in Kathmandu at noon local time yesterday.
In a statement today, the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma) said the team completed its arrival procedures and mission protocols by 4.30 pm local time, including logistics clearance and member manifest verification.
“As of the latest update, the team is en route to the Malaysian Embassy to receive a briefing on the current situation.
“Further coordination will be carried out with the Embassy and local emergency management agencies to determine the team’s deployment arrangements,” Nadma said.
The agency added that Nadma and the Malaysian Embassy in Nepal will coordinate daily mission reports for the duration of the operation.
Nadma also confirmed that all team members are in good health, with no issues reported as of the latest update.
Malaysia’s SMART MAS01 team in Kathmandu receive a briefing in Kathmandu to assist Nepal with humanitarian aid for the flood disaster on September 6, 2026. — Picture from Facebook/Bernama
The media previously reported that 11 SMART personnel departed for Nepal yesterday at 9 am aboard a Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) A400M aircraft from the Subang Air Base.
Also onboard were 12.4 tonnes of equipment, including rescue gear, detection devices, communication systems, high-capacity drone technology, and specialised tunnel rescue tools, along with a four-wheel-drive vehicle and a 10-tonne cargo truck. — Bernama

Title: Construction worker dies in Penang after seven-metre fall at Bayan Lepas site
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Sept 6 — A worker was killed after falling about seven metres while dismantling scaffolding at a construction site in Bayan Lepas here last Friday.
The Penang Department of Occupational Safety and Health (DOSH), in a statement today, said initial investigations found the incident occurred at 1.30 pm, when the victim was descending the scaffolding to take a lunch break.
“While descending the scaffolding, the victim fell from a height of about seven metres onto the floor.
“As a result of the incident, the victim sustained serious head injuries and was taken to Penang Hospital (HPP) for treatment but was pronounced dead,” it said.
Following the incident, Penang DOSH issued a stop work order and a prohibition of interference order to preserve the scene and ensure that investigations could be carried out smoothly.
DOSH said further investigations were underway, including recording statements from the employer and witnesses, to identify the cause of the accident and determine the level of compliance with occupational safety and health legislation.
The investigation is being conducted under Sections 15, 18A and 18B of the Occupational Safety and Health Act 1994 (Act 514), as well as the relevant occupational safety and health regulations. — Bernama

Title: Breathing isn’t easy in Kuching, Malaysia’s haziest spot at 10am as API hits 223
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 6 — Two areas in Sarawak recorded very unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as at 10am today, with Kuching recording the highest reading nationwide at 223, followed by Sri Aman at 215.
The Air Pollutant Index Management System (Apims) portal reported unhealthy API readings for 35 areas in eight states and three Federal Territories.
Sarawak recorded the highest number with 10 areas, followed by Selangor with six, Johor with four, Negeri Sembilan and Sabah with three each, and Pahang and Melaka with two each.
Kuala Lumpur also recorded two areas with unhealthy API readings, while Terengganu, Putrajaya and Labuan each recorded one.
In Sarawak, unhealthy air quality was recorded in Samalaju at 200, Bintulu at 198, Mukah at 194, Samarahan at 192, Sarikei at 188, IPD Serian and ILP Miri at 182 each, Sibu at 181 and Miri at 175.
In Selangor, the areas with unhealthy API readings were Johan Setia at 180, Shah Alam at 168, Banting and Petaling Jaya at 157 each, and Klang and Kuala Selangor at 154 each.
In Kuala Lumpur, Cheras recorded an API reading of 163 while Batu Muda recorded 161, while Putrajaya recorded 163.
In Pahang, Jerantut recorded an API reading of 168 while Temerloh recorded 164.
In Negeri Sembilan, Nilai recorded 167, Seremban 166 and Port Dickson 152.
In Johor, the areas with unhealthy API readings were Segamat at 160, Tangkak at 152, Kluang at 148 and Batu Pahat at 133.
In Sabah, Politeknik Kota Kinabalu recorded 164, Kota Kinabalu 161 and Kimanis 154, while Labuan recorded 161.
In Melaka, Alor Gajah and Bukit Rambai each recorded an API reading of 156.
In Terengganu, Paka recorded an unhealthy API reading of 107.
Other areas recorded good to moderate API readings.
An API reading of 0 to 50 indicates good air quality; 51 to 100, moderate; 101 to 200, unhealthy; 201 to 300, very unhealthy; and above 300, hazardous.

Title: Varsity student dies, eight in hospital after UiTM endurance challenge in Jengka
Article:
KUANTAN, Sept 6 — One participant died while eight others received treatment at hospital after experiencing health problems while taking part in the Komander Kesatria Endurance Challenge (KKEC) 2026 at Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM) in Jengka, Maran.
Maran Police chief Supt Wong Kim Wai said police received a report on the incident at 6.59 pm yesterday.
“The deceased was a 21-year-old male student. Further details will be provided after the post-mortem report is received,” he told Bernama when contacted.
It is understood that all of them lost consciousness before being rushed to hospital, with their condition believed to have been due to the hot weather.
Meanwhile, UiTM Pahang branch, in a statement, expressed its profound sadness and extended its condolences to the family of the participant from UiTM Negeri Sembilan branch, the late Fadhlan Fakhry Solana Mohd Fellimal.
“The university management always prioritises the wellbeing of its members and is therefore giving its full attention to the welfare of the deceased’s family.
“The management has mobilised comprehensive assistance to ensure that all matters relating to the funeral arrangements, documentation, transportation and emotional support for the family are handled smoothly and with ease,” the statement said.
UiTM said that, as part of its commitment to the safety and health of its students, the organisers had cancelled the outdoor events for KKEC 2026 scheduled for today.
According to the statement, the annual programme, which brings together kesatria commanders from all UiTM branches nationwide, is being held from Sept 2 to 8 at UiTM Pahang branch, Jengka Campus, and has been conducted in accordance with strict health and safety standard operating procedures (SOPs).
“All participants are required to undergo health screenings before the programme begins, as well as periodic health checks before each event. In fact, several participants had previously been asked to withdraw after failing the final screening,” it said.
The university said it takes the incident very seriously and will continue to closely monitor the situation to ensure the wellbeing of all those involved.
“We deeply regret any inconvenience caused, and greatly appreciate the cooperation and prayers of all parties as we navigate this difficult time,” it said. — Bernama

Title: Negeri Sembilan MB Ismail Lasim stands by Tuanku Muhriz amid fresh royal succession claim
Article:
SEREMBAN, Sept 6 — Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Haji Ismail Lasim today reaffirmed his support and loyalty to Yang di-Pertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz ibni Almarhum Tuanku Munawir amid an ongoing dispute over the state’s royal succession.
Ismail said he had taken note of a statement by the Undang Yang Empat – the hereditary chiefs of the four principal districts of Sungai Ujong, Jelebu, Johol and Rembau – and stressed that his priority was to discharge his responsibilities as menteri besar in the interests of the people and the state.
“I take note of the statement by Their Highnesses the Undang Yang Empat dated September 5, 2026.
“Whatever views expressed by Their Highnesses the Undang Yang Empat are their right.
“My focus now is to carry out my responsibilities as Menteri Besar Negeri Sembilan in the interests of the people and the state.
“Together with the state government, I express my full support and loyalty to His Royal Highness Tuanku Muhriz ibni Almarhum Tuanku Munawir as Yang di-Pertuan Besar Negeri Sembilan,” he said in a statement on his Facebook page today.
Ismail’s statement comes after the Undang Yang Empat, Tunku Besar Tampin and Datuk Shahbandar Sungai Ujong claimed that he had signed a proclamation on August 3 to give effect to the purported removal of Tuanku Muhriz.
In a joint statement yesterday, they alleged that Tuanku Nadzaruddin ibni Almarhum Tuanku Jaafar had received Ismail at Istana Laguna Biru in Port Dickson on August 3, where the menteri besar purportedly signed and completed the proclamation.
They claimed the document was made under Article 10(2) of the Negeri Sembilan Constitution and followed a proclamation signed and sealed by the Undang Yang Empat on April 19 declaring the removal of Tuanku Muhriz.
The group urged the proclamation to be enforced immediately, saying this was necessary to uphold the rule of law and the supremacy of the state constitution.
Ismail was sworn in as menteri besar on August 2 before Tuanku Muhriz, a day after Barisan Nasional won the state election.
The dispute began in April when the four Undang purportedly declared the removal of Tuanku Muhriz under Article 10(1)(b) of the state constitution and announced Tunku Nadzaruddin as the new Yang di-Pertuan Besar, a move not recognised by the state government.
The matter subsequently went to the High Court in Seremban, which on June 5 barred the six individuals involved from convening or holding Dewan Keadilan dan Undang meetings pending the court proceedings.
The dispute has continued, with competing claims over several traditional posts, including the proclamation of Azrin Khairi as Undang Luak Jelebu on Aug 28, which was opposed by a group of Datuk Lembaga Luak Jelebu.

Title: US envoy rejects Hadi’s claim it offered to help shape Malaysian govt leadership
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 6 — The United States today rejected PAS president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang’s claim that Washington had offered to help topple Malaysia’s government, saying it has never sought to decide the country’s political leadership.
The US Embassy in Malaysia Chargé d’Affaires ad interim David H. Gamble Jr. said any suggestion that the United States had sought to determine Malaysia’s political leadership was untrue.
“The United States has never sought to decide Malaysia's political leadership.
“Any account to the contrary is false,” he said in a statement posted on its Facebook page.
The denial came a day after Abdul Hadi claimed that PAS leaders were offered assistance by a foreign power to topple and take over the government during former US president Barack Obama’s visit to Malaysia in 2014.
The PAS president said several party leaders had been invited to a meeting at the US Embassy while PAS was still part of the Pakatan Rakyat coalition.
He said then PAS assistant secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan and Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar, who was his political secretary at the time, attended the meeting.
Abdul Hadi said the embassy representatives had discussed the possibility of helping PAS topple and take over the government, but the party leaders rejected any such foreign interference.
He also claimed that the US ambassador later met him separately and asked whom PAS was proposing as prime minister.
Abdul Hadi said he responded by asking whom the United States supported, before later recounting the exchange to former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad, who he said approved of his response.
Takiyuddin separately confirmed attending the embassy meeting, saying PAS had rejected foreign interference in Malaysia’s politics.
He said the embassy representative had asked whether PAS planned to topple the Barisan Nasional (BN) government at the time, but the party made no decision because it did not want foreign countries interfering in the country’s affairs.
BN was eventually defeated in the 2018 general election, when Pakatan Harapan won power after a campaign heavily focused on the 1MDB scandal and corruption allegations involving then prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak.

Title: Miri’s landslide-prone roads on Canada Hill set for RM30 million rebuild in 2027
Article:
MIRI, Sept 6 — A RM30 million special allocation has been approved under the 13th Malaysia Plan (13MP) to reconstruct Jalan Canada Hill to the Grand Old Lady here, and the access road to Kampung Padang Kerbau, with construction expected to kick off next year.
According to State Transport Minister Dato Sri Lee Kim Shin, the project is currently at the consultancy assessment and design stage, with the final engineering solution to be determined after detailed assessments by appointed consultants and professional engineers.
He said the project would involve the reconstruction and possible widening of the roads, although the exact engineering approach had yet to be finalised due to the challenging terrain and recurring landslides in the area.
“At the moment, we cannot determine what method will ultimately be used to improve the affected sections, including whether the road foundation needs to be reconstructed and the road widened, or whether a bridge structure needs to be built at certain sections.
“All these decisions can only be made after the professional design is completed.
“We do not know exactly how they will do it. They may build foundations at some sections, construct bridges at others, or adopt another method.
“Everything depends on the engineers’ design,” he said during an inspection of Canada Hill on Friday.
Lee explained that the conditions along the affected roads were challenging and could not simply be addressed through conventional road repair methods.
He said should landslides recur after the repairs, the affected sections would have to be dealt with again, underscoring the need for a professional engineering design.
However, Lee stressed that immediate action would still be taken to address dangerous sections while awaiting implementation of the RM30 million reconstruction project.
The Senadin assemblyman said the Jalan Canada Hill-Grand Old Lady was under the responsibility of Miri City Council (MCC) for maintenance and upkeep.
“However, as the landslide-affected sections have deteriorated, I have asked the Public Works Department to prepare an estimate (quotation) first, after which the relevant road management committee will decide whether emergency funding can be sought to repair the affected sections,” he said.
Lee said the road leading to the Petroleum Science Museum was particularly challenging and should not be treated as a routine road maintenance issue.
He added that the city council had previously received complaints and carried out repairs on some landslide-affected sections, but several of the repaired areas subsequently deteriorated.
“Therefore, I have asked the Public Works Department to assist and expedite emergency funding to address the more dangerous sections first,” he said. —- The Borneo Post
